final_notes: Models: RESGA and SAEGA. Per-task (full) scores — RESGA: [49.86, 50.63, 62.65, 45.12, 41.46, 51.22, 38.50, 38.50, 34.50, 45.83]; SAEGA: [49.84, 49.95, 70.70, 46.95, 40.85, 49.14, 31.50, 40.50, 38.50, 46.44]. Mechanistic claims: SAEGA neutralizes sycophancy (instance-wise neutrality: sharp low-variance peak at zero on sycophancy projection); RESGA and dense steering produce mean shifts while retaining variance. Sparsity: baseline ≈50 active SAE features/token; dense steering >150; RESGA slightly increases sparsity; SAEGA preserves sparsity (~50–60). Feature-level: SAEGA suppresses sycophancy-related SAE features. PCA: dense steering exits manifold; RESGA causes a high-variance shift; SAEGA stays in a tight orthogonal subspace. Prompt findings: Table 2 — random-init discovered prompts often non-linguistic; Table 3 — seed-initialized EPO yields more interpretable prompts and reductions from seed→optimized. WikiText2 perplexities (Table 4): Llama 12.56→12.07, Qwen 10.88→12.48, Gemma 30.51→29.19; changes described as negligible though Qwen increases. Ablations (Table 5): reported Random Direction, Random Mutation, Task Loss numbers across Sycophancy/Hallucination/MyopicReward (example Random Direction Sycophancy 74.13/84.56/81.47; Task Loss Sycophancy 55.83/73.50/58.70). Conclusions: claim interpretable control; significant improvement on sycophancy and myopic reward; consistent hallucination improvements; outperform manual prompting and dense steering. Limitations: labeled data required; SAE latents and steering vectors are model-specific (need retraining per model); fluency-effectiveness tradeoff — top prompts often lack semantic coherence. Broader impact: method intended to improve LLM safety by suppressing undesired personas but could be adapted to target safety-critical SAE latents (risking automated jailbreak discovery); deployment should use access controls. Acknowledgment: used Claude (Anthropic) for manuscript writing assistance and AI-assisted code generation.

Title/authors: Gradient-ascent based prompt discovery for interpretable persona control — Harshvardhan Saini, Yiming Tang, Dianbo Liu. Methods: RESGA (constructs persona steering vectors from residual-stream / dense representation differences) and SAEGA (uses SAE-discovered latents as interpretable persona features). Both use a "fluent gradient ascent" procedure to discover natural-language prompts with controllable fluency. Tasks/models: steer three personas — sycophancy, hallucination, myopic reward — evaluated on Llama 3.1, Qwen 2.5, Gemma 3. Claims: automatically discovered prompts significantly improve sycophancy and myopic reward versus manual prompting and dense (activation) steering (Sec 4.2); representation-level evidence claimed that prompt-based steering avoids distributional shifts caused by dense steering. Repo: github.com/HarshSaini10/RESGA_SAEGA. Related work summary from this part: persona-steering prior work includes RLHF and Constitutional AI; Representation Engineering (RepE) and Contrastive Activation Addition (CAA) extract/apply concept directions/steering vectors; activation steering shown to mitigate sycophancy/toxicity/bias; Wang et al. (2025) report SAE latents capture persona features usable via activation clamping. SAEs: cited as introduced in Cunningham et al. (2023b); SAEs can reveal monosemantic neurons and reduce superposition; related techniques include JumpReLU, Top-K, Batch Top-K, Matryoshka SAEs; LLM-based analyses and subpopulation inspection often used to interpret SAE neurons. Prompt-engineering context: GPT-3, chain-of-thought, self-consistency, PAL/PoT, evolutionary prompt optimization (EPO), Greedy Coordinate Gradient (GCG), ProTeGi, and theoretical framing viewing prompting as optimal control. Caveats to check later: (1) paper has earlier inconsistent language about optimization objective (maximize vs steer away), (2) abstract sycophancy percentages ambiguous (49.90% vs 79.24%), (3) ensure evidence supports claim that prompt-based steering avoids distributional shifts from dense steering.

steps.notes_before: Paper: RESGA & SAEGA for persona steering. Section 3 overview: pipeline (text says three-stage: 1) construct steering vectors, 2) fluent gradient ascent to discover prompts, 3) initialize/select prompts), but Figure 2 caption describes only two stages (vector construction + optimization) and shows an inconsistent objective form (see errors). Persona steering vectors: Representation-based (Eq.1) v_repr = mean_{D+} e(x) - mean_{D-} e(x). SAE-based (Eq.2): select top-K latents I_K by |mean activation difference|; v_SAE = sum_{i in I_K} w_i * (bar a_i^+ - bar a_i^-), with a_i(x)=ReLU(w_i e(x)+b_i) and w_i row of W_enc. Persona reduction objective: f(t) = - <e(t), v> / ||e(t)|| (Eq.3); text: maximize f to push representations away from persona direction. Fluency-regularized objective: Eq.(4) L_lambda(t) = f(t) - (lambda/n) sum_{i} H(m(prefix), next_token), where H is cross-entropy; note this conflicts with Figure 2's stated L_lambda = f + H. Optimization: use Evolutionary Prompt Optimization (EPO) — population M, fluency weights {lambda_i}, prompt length n, gradient magnitudes to pick top-k token candidates per position, mutate by token replacement, periodic restarts, select best per lambda to span Pareto frontier.

final_notes: Methods & main quantitative rows: RESGA ≈ [49.86, 50.63, 62.65, 45.12, 41.46, 51.22, 38.50, 38.50, 34.50, 45.83]; SAEGA ≈ [49.84, 49.95, 70.70, 46.95, 40.85, 49.14, 31.50, 40.50, 38.50, 46.44]. Paper claim: both methods largely neutralize sycophancy (~50%) and improve myopic reward/hallucination metrics, but results are mixed: WikiText2 perplexities (Table 4) Llama 12.56→12.07 (improve), Gemma 30.51→29.19 (improve), Qwen 10.88→12.48 (worse). Table 3 (seed vs optimized prompts): some seeds improved (71.15%→54.22%, 72.06%→51.72%), but at least one optimized prompt increased sycophancy (52.43%→59.35%). Table 2: many discovered prompts are gibberish; seed-initialized EPO yields more interpretable prompts. Mechanistic findings: RESGA induces token-priming via induction heads; SAEGA yields a sharp neutral peak, preserves activation manifolds, and steers via semantic feature-level control (suppresses agreement tokens, upweights contrast tokens like “However/But”). SAEGA is sparse (~50–60 active features/token) vs dense steering (>150 active features/token). Both methods upweight long-term tokens tied to myopic reward. Ablations (Table 5): replacing persona steering vector with Random Direction worsens sycophancy (Llama 74.13, Qwen 84.56, Gemma 81.47); Random Mutation and Task-Loss-as-Objective underperform vs representation-based, gradient-guided methods. Limitations: labeled data required for RESGA/SAEGA; SAE latents and steering vectors are model-specific and require retraining per target model; most effective prompts lack semantic coherence (fluency vs effectiveness tradeoff). Broader impact: pipeline could be adapted to target safety-critical SAE latents (jailbreaks/harmful outputs); recommend access controls. Acknowledgment: used Claude (Anthropic) for manuscript writing assistance and AI-assisted code generation.

final_notes: Tasks: B2R (soph.), U9K (halluc.; TruthfulQA MC), D6V (myopic reward). Metric: lower = better (fraction preferring undesirable option). Models: C7N = Llama3.1-8B, W4X = Qwen2.5-7B, F9S = Gemma3-4B. Key results: Table1 per-model (QX2 B2R): C7N 49.86, W4X 50.63, F9S 62.65; (V7P) C7N 49.84, W4X 49.95, F9S 70.70. Table3: random seeds ~69–72% undesirable, optimized prompts ~46–59% (optimized better). Table4 (WikiText2 perplexities): C7N 12.56→12.07, W4X 10.88→12.48 (increase), F9S 30.51→29.19. Mechanisms: QX2 = label/head-token priming (Y2H); V7P = semantic/vocab steering via ΔLogits (G6T). V7P produces a 'polite disagreement' signature (suppresses "Yes/True/Agree", upweights "However/But"); QX2 and V7P upweight long-term/planning words on D6V. Ablations (Table5): random persona direction K3Y much worse (e.g., K3Y B2R: 74.13, 84.56, 81.47); random mutation E8U degrades performance; task-loss M5A unstable and usually underperforms QX2/V7P. Noted internal inconsistency (earlier): the paper asserts V7P causes a sharp collapse-to-neutrality but Table5 includes a large F9S V7P outlier (70.70), which contradicts collapse claim. Conclusion & future work: semi-supervised label reduction, cross-model transferability of prompts, multi-persona steering. Limitations: QX2/V7P require examples showing and lacking the persona; SAE latents/steering vectors are model-specific (need retraining); most effective prompts lack semantic coherence. Broader impact: dual-use/jailbreak risks; recommend access controls. Acknowledgment: Claude (Anthropic) assisted with manuscript writing and AI-assisted code generation.

steps.notes_before: Three-stage method: (i) persona-vector construction, (ii) fluency-constrained discovery, (iii) initialization/frontier selection via validation. Persona vectors: v_repr = (1/|D+|) sum_{x in D+} e(x) - (1/|D-|) sum_{x in D-} e(x) (eq 1). SAE alternative: v_SAE = sum_{i in I_K} w_i * (\bar a_i^+ - \bar a_i^-), with a_i(x)=ReLU(w_i e(x)+b_i) and \bar a^+,\bar a^- means over D^+,D^- (eq 2). Persona-reduction objective: f(t) = -<e(t),v>/||e(t)|| (eq 3) — maximizing f pushes representations away from the persona direction (reduces persona). Fluency control: objective L_λ balances f and next-token cross-entropy H; however the paper gives two inconsistent forms — a caption L_λ = f + H and Eq. (4) L_λ = f - (λ/n) sum_i H(m(t_{≤i}), t_{i+1}) (the latter includes sign and λ/n scaling). Algorithm: N8C (population M, per-candidate λ_i) uses gradients on one-hot token encodings, top-k token selection per position, random-token mutation, periodic restarts, and selects prompts across the fluency–steering Pareto frontier. Initialization: natural-language seeds (e.g., "Please answer honestly" for B2R) bias search toward higher-fluency frontier regions; candidates are appended to validation inputs and selected by downstream behavioral metric. Frontier analysis prefers intermediate prompts balancing steering and moderate perplexity increases; fluency here is self cross-entropy (no hard threshold).

final_notes: Summary: V7P described as precise, sparse, semantically grounded vs P8D's global interference. Neutralization: QX2 shifts B2R mean toward neutrality with high variance; V7P claimed to cause variance collapse to near-neutrality (instance-wise neutrality — "statistically indistinguishable from random choice"). Contradiction: V7P is also reported to systematically suppress agreement tokens ("Yes","True","Agree") and upweight contrastive tokens ("However","But") and to upweight long-term planning lexicon ("Future","Long","Wait"). SAE L0 sparsity: P8D inflates feature counts; QX2 partially increases sparsity; V7P preserves baseline L0 (~50). Residual PCA: P8D = large off-manifold displacement; QX2 = high-variance mean shift; V7P = tight, stable region often orthogonal to P8D. Table issues: Table 3 seed vs optimized prompt wording inconsistent; Table 4 reports W4X perplexity rising (10.88→12.48) despite "negligible" claim. Mechanisms: Y2H for QX2; G6T and ΔLogits for V7P. Ablations (Table 5): K3Y/E8U degrade; M5A unstable and underperforms QX2/V7P. Selected metrics (lower better): QX2 B2R: 49.86/50.63/62.65; V7P B2R: 49.84/49.95/70.70. New final-part content: Conclusion lists semi-supervised labeled-data reduction, cross-model transferability, multi-persona steering as future work. Limitations note QX2/V7P require labeled examples, SAE latents are model-specific, and effective prompts often lack semantic coherence. Broader impact warns of dual-use; acknowledgment credits Claude (Anthropic).

Abstract claims: methods QX2 and V7P optimize randomly initialized prompts toward identified persona directions via gradient ascent; J4Z controls discovered-prompt fluency. Method mapping: QX2 = RESGA (RESidual Gradient Ascent) — dense residual-stream optimization using direct representation differences to construct undesired-persona directions; V7P = SAEGA (Sparse Autoencoder Gradient Ascent) — latent-based optimization identifying causally relevant SAE features. Both maximize departure from undesired directions with controllable prompt fluency; mechanistic guidance replaces black-box search. Background: SAEs decompose activations into interpretable features; gradient-ascent visualization in CNNs motivates continuous opt; discrete-language issues (off-manifold tokens, polysemanticity) and prior evolutionary/token-replacement work found adversarial/jailbreak prompts, not model-steering prompts.

steps.notes_before: Paper: RESGA/SAEGA persona-control via discovered soft prompts. Three-stage method: (1) persona-vector construction, (2) fluency-constrained prompt discovery, (3) initialization/frontier selection via validation. Persona vectors: dense representation difference v_repr = mean_{D+} e(x) - mean_{D-} e(x) (eq (1)); SAE alternative v_SAE = sum_{i in I_K} w_i * (\bar a_i^+ - \bar a_i^-) where a_i(x)=ReLU(w_i e(x)+b_i) (eq (2)). Persona-reduction objective f(t) = -<e(t),v>/||e(t)|| using last-token activation (eq (3)); maximize f to move representations away from persona. Fluency-regularized objective reported in eq (4) as L_λ(t)=f(t) - (λ/n) sum_i H(m(t_{<=i}), t_{i+1}) to be maximized (λ controls steering–fluency tradeoff). Optimization uses an evolutionary, gradient-guided population algorithm (Algorithm 1): M candidates with distinct λ_i, compute gradients, pick top-k token substitutions per position, mutate, select best, periodic restarts. Initialization: random or short natural-language seeds (e.g., "Please answer honestly" for B2R); select prompts by change in held-out behavioral metric and prefer intermediate-frontier tradeoffs. final_notes:
Methods: three-stage persona steering (RESGA = representation-difference; SAEGA = SAE-based sparse steering). Prompt optimization via EPO (M=100, n=8, T=1000). Models/eval: Llama 3.1 8B, Qwen 2.5 7B, Gemma 3 4B. Target layers: Llama/Qwen layer 25, Gemma layer 20. SAEGA: K=20; natural sparsity L0 ≈ 50.
Main quantitative (Table 1; lower better avg): RESGA 45.83, SAEGA 46.44, Standard Prompt 55.45, Dense Steering 56.10. Table 3: example seed→optimized drop 69.16 → 56.25. Perplexity (WikiText2, Table 4): Llama 12.56 → 12.07 (improve); Qwen 10.88 → 12.48 (worse); Gemma 30.51 → 29.19 (improve).
Qualitative (Table 2): discovered prompts often lack semantic coherence. Mechanistic findings: induction-head token-priming effects; SAEGA suppresses affirmations ("Yes/True/Agree") and upweights contrast tokens ("However/But"); RESGA+SAEGA upweight long-term tokens for Myopic Reward. Activation geometry: neutrality around 0.0; baseline active features ≈50, dense steering >150, SAEGA ≈50–60.
Ablations (Table 5): Random Direction sometimes outperforms Zero-Shot (examples: 84.56 < 86.00, 81.47 < 82.00), so improvements are not uniformly consistent.
Limitations: RESGA/SAEGA need labeled examples per target persona; SAE latents and steering vectors are model-specific and must be retrained per model; fluency-effectiveness tradeoff (most effective prompts are incoherent); adding linguistic priors suggested.
Broader impact: aim to improve safety by suppressing undesired personas, but pipeline could be misused for jailbreak/harmful-output discovery; recommend access controls. Acknowledgement: used Claude (Anthropic) for manuscript writing assistance and code generation.

Paper studies automatic prompt discovery for controlling behavioral personas in LLMs. Introduces RESGA (RESidual Gradient Ascent) using dense residual representations and SAEGA (Sparse Autoencoder Gradient Ascent) using sparse autoencoder features. Both build persona directions from contrasting examples and optimize prompts subject to a fluency constraint. Experiments target sycophancy (agreement with incorrect user opinion), hallucination (evaluated via TruthfulQA error), and myopic reward (short-term reward seeking over long-term outcomes). Reports improvements on Llama 3.1, Qwen 2.5, and Gemma 3. Abstract states a sycophancy improvement of 49.90% compared with 79.24% (numbers noted as presented). Mechanistic analyses claim SAEGA suppresses relevant features, concentrates behavior near neutrality, and preserves natural activation sparsity. Limitations listed: need for labeled data, steering directions that are model-specific, and prompt coherence issues.

Paper studies automatic prompt discovery to steer behavioral personas (sycophancy, hallucination via TruthfulQA, myopic reward) using RESGA (RESidual Gradient Ascent: dense residual steering vector v_repr from mean-representation differences) and SAEGA (Sparse Autoencoder Gradient Ascent: steering via selected SAE encoder directions v_SAE). Persona directions are built from contrast sets D+ (persona-exhibiting) and D- (persona-free). SAE latents a_i(x) use an encoder W_enc, rows w_i, ReLU and bias b_i; top-K latents I_K selected by |\bar a_i^+ - \bar a_i^-|. The persona-reduction objective f(t) is the negative scaled projection of the prompt representation e(t) onto v; combined objective L_\lambda(t)=f(t)+\lambda H (H = self cross-entropy under model m) balances steering and fluency. Evolutionary Prompt Optimization (EPO) optimizes discrete prompts with population M, prompt length n, iterations T, candidate-replacement size k (gradient-guided selection vs random mutation), restarts, and random/seed initialization. Fluency is measured by prompt self cross-entropy; WikiText2 perplexity is reported for language-modeling. Evaluation: sycophancy error rate (undesirable preference; neutralization=50%), instance-wise neutrality = near-zero, low-variance projections attributed to SAEGA; behavioral reversal = beyond neutrality. Models: Llama 3.1 8B, Qwen 2.5 7B, Gemma 3 4B. Baselines include Zero-Shot, Standard Prompt, Dense Steering Vector, Random Direction, Task Loss objective, and ProTeGi (GPT-4o). Mechanistic claims: SAEGA suppresses persona features, preserves natural sparse topology; RESGA often shifts mean projections (distributional shifting). Table references: Avg. in Table 1; literal optimized prompts in Tables 2–3. Abstract reported sycophancy numbers ~49.90% vs 79.24%.

(2) Fluent gradient-ascent prompt search optimizing persona-reduction f(t) and fluency. f(t) = -<e(t),v>/||e(t)|| where e(t) is last-token representation (Eq.3). EPO algorithm: population M with per-prompt fluency weights {λ_i}; initialize M prompts length n; iterate T times: compute L_{λ_i} and gradients w.r.t. one-hot encodings, pick top-k candidate tokens per position by gradient magnitude, mutate by replacing a random token with sampled top-k alternatives, evaluate and keep best per λ_i; periodic restarts retain one best and reinit others. final_notes: Methods: RESGA and SAEGA build steering vectors from labeled examples and optimize prompts via evolutionary gradient ascent for interpretable control. Key numbers: Table 1 (Avg col) — RESGA 45.83, SAEGA 46.44, Standard Prompt 55.45, Dense Steering Vector 56.10 (text sometimes claims RESGA/SAEGA outperform manual/dense despite these values). Per-model (Table 5) examples — Sycophancy: RESGA [Llama 49.86, Qwen 50.63, Gemma 62.65]; SAEGA [49.84, 49.95, 70.70]. Hallucination: RESGA [45.12, 41.46, 51.22]; SAEGA [46.95, 40.85, 49.14]. Myopic Reward: RESGA [38.50, 38.50, 34.50]; SAEGA [31.50, 40.50, 38.50]. Ablations: Random Direction collapses; Random Mutation degrades performance; Task-loss objective unstable/worse. Example seed→optimized reduction (Table 3): 69.16→56.25. WikiText2 perplexities: Llama 12.56→12.07 (small decrease), Qwen 10.88→12.48 (increase), Gemma 30.51→29.19 (small decrease); paper elsewhere calls perplexity changes 'negligible' which conflicts with Qwen's increase. Conclusions/claims to check: neutrality near 0.0; baseline active features ≈50; dense steering >150; SAEGA ≈50–60; claims that SAEGA neutralizes behavior conflict with SAEGA's high Gemma sycophancy (70.70). Limitations: labeled-data requirement; SAE latents and steering vectors are model-specific and need per-model retraining; fluency-effectiveness tradeoff — many effective prompts lack semantic coherence. Broader impact: authors state the pipeline could be misused to target safety-critical SAE latents, automate jailbreak/harmful-output elicitation, and recommend access controls. Paper introduces two methods for automatic persona prompt discovery: RESGA (RESidual Gradient Ascent) using dense residual representations, and SAEGA (Sparse Autoencoder Gradient Ascent) using sparse autoencoder features. Both build persona directions from contrasting examples and optimize prompts under a fluency constraint. Experiments target three failure modes: sycophancy (defined as agreement with an incorrect user opinion), hallucination (measured via TruthfulQA error), and myopic reward (short-term reward seeking over long-term outcomes). Reported empirical scope: improvements across Llama 3.1, Qwen 2.5, and Gemma 3. Abstract gives a sycophancy improvement reported as 49.90% compared with 79.24% (ambiguous phrasing—both numbers noted). Mechanistic findings for SAEGA: suppresses relevant features, concentrates behavior near neutrality, and preserves natural activation sparsity. Limitations listed: requires labeled data, steering directions are model-specific, and prompt coherence issues.

Methods: RESGA (RESidual Gradient Ascent) uses dense residual representations (v_repr constructed from mean representation differences D+, D-). SAEGA (Sparse Autoencoder Gradient Ascent) constructs v_SAE from top-K SAE encoder directions (W_enc rows w_i; activations a_i(x); means \bar a_i^+, \bar a_i^-). SAE latents use ReLU + bias b_i; SAE-Lens provides pretrained SAEs. Optimization: Evolutionary Prompt Optimization (EPO) — gradient-guided evolutionary token-replacement (k candidate tokens per position selected by gradient magnitude), population M, iterations T, nearest-token projection to discrete tokens, restarts (keep best prompt under random λ), seed and random initializations. Objective: f(t) is negative scaled projection of prompt representation e(t) onto steering vector v (projection numerator uses ⟨·,·⟩ and is scaled by ∥e(t)∥); combined L_λ(t)=steering+λ·H where H is prompt self cross-entropy (fluency measured by model m). Fluency measured both by self cross-entropy and reported perplexity on WikiText2. Ablations: random mutation, random direction, task-loss-as-objective. Evaluation: three failure modes — sycophancy (agreement with incorrect user opinion), hallucination (TruthfulQA multiple-choice; lower error = better factuality), myopic reward (short-term reward seeking). Metrics: error rate = fraction preferring undesirable option; neutralization for sycophancy = 50% error (no systematic agreement/disagreement); behavioral reversal = beyond 50%. Empirical scope: Llama 3.1 8B Instruct, Qwen 2.5 7B Instruct, Gemma 3 4B Instruct. Mechanistic findings: SAEGA suppresses relevant features, concentrates behavior near neutrality (instance-wise near-zero, low-variance), preserves natural sparse topology (L0 sparsity), suppresses agreement markers ("Yes","True","Agree") and upweights pivots ("However","But"); RESGA/SAEGA upweight long-term tokens ("Future","Long","Wait"). Diagnostics: ΔLogits = Logits_steered - Logits_baseline; PCA visualizations and steering trajectories reported.

steps.notes_before: Framework: three stages — (1) build persona steering vector (RESGA via representation mean-difference; SAEGA via SAE latents), (2) fluent gradient-ascent prompt discovery, (3) initialize/select prompts on Pareto frontier. RESGA: v_repr = mean_{D+} e(x) - mean_{D-} e(x). SAEGA: select top-K latents by |mean activation difference|; v_SAE = sum_{i in I_K} w_i*(\bar a_i^+ - \bar a_i^-), where a_i(x)=ReLU(w_i e(x)+b_i) and w_i is SAE encoder row i. Steering objective: f(t)= -<e(t),v>/||e(t)|| (negative scaled projection of last-token representation). Fluency term: cross-entropy H(m(prefix), next_token). Paper contains an internal inconsistency: Figure 2 writes L_λ(t)=f(t)+H(t), but Eq. (4) defines L_λ(t)=f(t) - (λ/n) sum_i H(...), i.e. opposite sign and includes λ/n normalization. EPO (Evolutionary Prompt Optimization): maintains M prompts each with fluency weight λ_i, runs T iterations, computes gradients w.r.t. one-hot token encodings, selects top-k candidate tokens per position by gradient magnitude, generates mutations by replacing a random token with a sampled top-k alternative, evaluates candidates and keeps best per λ_i, with periodic restarts (retain best under random λ, reinitialize others). Prior notes: tasks (sycophancy, hallucination TruthfulQA, myopic reward), models (Llama 3.1 8B, Qwen 2.5 7B, Gemma 3 4B), Table 1 averages and per-model RESGA/SAEGA numbers recorded earlier for cross-checking.

final_notes: Paper: RESGA and SAEGA for persona steering. Methods: RESGA = steering vector from representation differences. SAEGA = select top-K SAE latents (K=20) and sum weighted mean activation diffs. Prompt optimization: evolutionary gradient ascent (EPO) with M=100, prompt length n=8, T=1000; two inits (random tokens or seed natural phrase). Models: Llama 3.1 8B, Qwen 2.5 7B, Gemma 3 4B. Intervention layers: L25 for Llama/Qwen, L20 for Gemma. Eval metric: fraction preferring undesirable option (lower better); sycophancy neutral=50%. Reported metric rows: RESGA = [49.86, 50.63, 62.65, 45.12, 41.46, 51.22, 38.50, 38.50, 34.50]. SAEGA = [49.84, 49.95, 70.70, 46.95, 40.85, 49.14, 31.50, 40.50, 38.50]. Mechanistic claims: RESGA acts via token-priming induction heads; SAEGA produces semantic steering (suppresses agreement tokens, upweights pivots like 'However' and long-term tokens). Ablations (Table 5): random baselines and task-loss objectives degrade performance versus proposed methods. Limitations: labeled data required; SAE latents and steering vectors are model-specific (need retraining per model); fluency-effectiveness tradeoff—most effective prompts lack semantic coherence. Noted internal inconsistencies earlier in paper: claim of consistent hallucination improvements conflicts with reported hallucination numbers (RESGA 62.65, SAEGA 70.70 higher); claim SAEGA preserves activation manifolds contradicts statement SAEGA 'collapses variance toward zero'; Table 4 claim of negligible perplexity change conflicts with Qwen perplexity increase 10.88 -> 12.48. Broader impact (this part): pipeline could be misused to target safety-critical SAE latents (jailbreak discovery); recommend access controls. Acknowledgment: used Claude (Anthropic) for manuscript writing assistance and AI-assisted code generation.

steps.notes_before: Paper: "Gradient-ascent based prompt discovery for interpretable persona control" (Saini et al.). Methods: RESGA (representation-based steering) and SAEGA (SAE latent-based steering). Pipeline: (1) construct steering vector v in R^d (Sec 3.1), (2) discover prompts via fluent gradient ascent / EPO (Sec 3.2), (3) initialize/select prompts from Pareto frontier (Sec 3.3 forthcoming). Representation steering: v_repr = mean_{x in D+} e(x) - mean_{x in D-} e(x). SAE steering: pick top-K latents by |mean activation difference|; v_SAE = sum_{i in I_K} w_i * (\bar a_i^+ - \bar a_i^-), where w_i is row i of W_enc and a_i(x)=ReLU(w_i e(x)+b_i). Persona reduction objective: f(t) = -<e(t), v>/||e(t)|| (maximize to point away from persona). Fluency term H is cross-entropy of next-token probabilities. Internal inconsistency: Figure caption states L_\lambda = f + H, but Eq. (4) gives L_\lambda = f - (\lambda/n) sum H(·) (sign and scaling mismatch). EPO: population size M, prompt length n, different \lambda_i per member; algorithm uses gradients to pick top-k token substitutions, mutate, evaluate, restart; text claims gradients w.r.t. token embeddings but Alg. step 6 says gradients w.r.t. one-hot encodings (contradiction). Reported empirical note: EPO improves Llama myopic-reward error by 23.50 points vs random mutation. Keep these inconsistencies and the formulas for checking later claims (esp. objective sign and gradient computations).

Persona-reduction objective: f(t) = -<e(t), v>/||e(t)|| (optimize to point away from persona). Fluency term H is next-token cross-entropy of the prompt under the LM. Internal inconsistencies already noted: figure caption vs Eq.(4) give conflicting signs/scaling for L_\lambda (caption: L_\lambda = f + H; Eq.(4): L_\lambda = f - (\lambda/n) sum H(·)); algorithm text claims gradients w.r.t. token embeddings but Alg. step references gradients w.r.t. one-hot encodings. New from this part: two EPO initializations — random (uniform tokens, low fluency) and seed (short natural-language phrase related to persona, higher fluency). EPO yields candidate prompts spanning a Pareto frontier of steering strength vs model-based fluency (measured by prompt self cross-entropy). Evaluation: append prompt to inputs, measure change in target behavioral metric on held-out validation; emphasize intermediate frontier prompts balancing steering and moderate perplexity increases; assess prompt stability across validation examples. Note: fluency metric is model-intrinsic cross-entropy, not equated to human readability.

final_notes: Methods: QX2 = gradient-guided prompt search; V7P = SAE-based top-K latent steering. Models: C7N (Llama 3.1 8B), W4X (Qwen 2.5 7B), F9S (Gemma 3 4B). Tasks: B2R (sycophancy), U9K (hallucination/TruthfulQA MC), D6V (myopic reward). Key results (earlier tables): QX2 B2R ≈ 49.86, 50.63, 62.65 (C7N, W4X, F9S). V7P B2R ≈ 49.84, 49.95, 70.70 (F9S is an outlier showing much worse suppression). Ablations (Table 5): Random Direction (K3Y) B2R: C7N 74.13, W4X 84.56, F9S 81.47 (worse); Random Mutation (E8U) B2R: 68.00, 71.66, 76.04; Task-loss objective (M5A) B2R: 55.83, 73.50, 58.70. QX2 row (restate): 49.86, 50.63, 62.65; V7P row: 49.84, 49.95, 70.70. Flagged internal concerns to check later: (1) paper-level narrative claiming V7P 'systematically' suppresses agreement/upweights 'However/But' conflicts with F9S B2R=70.70 counterexample; (2) earlier notes about V7P causing variance collapse/neutrality appear inconsistent with any claims of consistently nuanced token steering. Current part (Conclusion, Limitations, Broader Impact, Acknowledgment): Conclusion lists future directions: semi-supervised labeled-data reduction, cross-model transferability of discovered prompts, multi-persona steering. Limitations: QX2 and V7P require positive and negative examples; SAE latents/steering vectors are model-specific and need retraining; most effective prompts lack semantic coherence (fluency–effectiveness tradeoff). Broader impact: intended for safety but could be misused (jailbreaks, harmful outputs). Acknowledgment: Claude (Anthropic) assisted writing and AI-assisted code generation. No new numeric claims here; Limitations and Conclusion are consistent (limitation noted, future work to address it).

steps.notes_before: Paper proposes gradient-guided discovery of interpretable persona-control prompts. Persona steering vectors: two options — direct representation difference v_repr = mean_{D+} e(x) - mean_{D-} e(x) (eq.1) and SAE-based v_SAE = sum_{i in I_K} w_i*(bar a_i^+ - bar a_i^-) with a_i(x)=ReLU(w_i e(x)+b_i) (eq.2). v is the suppression target direction in activation space (D+ exhibits persona, D- lacks it). Persona-reduction objective f(t) = -<e(t),v>/||e(t)|| (eq.3); maximizing f pushes representations away from v. Fluency-controlled objective L_λ(t)= f(t) - (λ/n) sum_i H(m(t_≤i), t_{i+1}) (eq.4) trades steering vs model cross-entropy (fluency/probability under model). Algorithm N8C: maintain M prompts with different λ_i, compute gradients wrt one-hot tokens, pick top-k per position, mutate by replacing tokens, periodic restarts, select best per λ. Evolutionary search claimed to improve C7N D6V error by 23.50 points over E8U. Initialization/selection: seed prompts (e.g. "Please answer honestly") bias search toward higher-fluency frontier; candidates appended to validation inputs and selected by downstream behavioral metric; examine performance across fluency frontier. Note: earlier parts apparently claim steering sometimes moves toward persona directions — unresolved contradiction with Section 3.2's 'move away' objective.

final_notes: Methods: RESGA (residual-based GA), SAEGA (SAE-based GA). EPO hyperparams: M=100, prompt length n=8, T=1000. SAE: sparsity L0 ≈50 active features; SAE K=20. Models: Llama 3.1 (8B), Qwen 2.5 (7B), Gemma 3 (4B). Results (Table1): Sycophancy — RESGA [49.86,50.63,62.65], SAEGA [49.84,49.95,70.70]; Hallucination — RESGA [45.12,41.46,51.22], SAEGA [46.95,40.85,49.14]; Myopic — RESGA [38.50,38.50,34.50], SAEGA [31.50,40.50,38.50]. Averages: RESGA 45.83, SAEGA 46.44. Baselines: Standard Prompt 55.45, Dense Steering 56.10. Perplexities (Table4) pre→post: Llama 12.56→12.07 (↓), Qwen 10.88→12.48 (↑), Gemma 30.51→29.19 (↓). Mechanisms: RESGA sometimes injects alternative-label tokens; SAEGA suppresses agreement tokens and upweights contrast/connective tokens; both upweight long-term-planning tokens. Ablations (Table5): Random Direction / Random Mutation / Task Loss perform worse; paper claims persona-direction steering essential and random mutation degrades, but an earlier note records a conflicting statement that SAEGA 'collapses variance' (direction-insensitive). Conclusions: discovered prompts improve persona metrics; SAEGA 'neutralizes' behavior and preserves natural activation manifolds (~50 active features vs >150 for dense). Limitations: require labeled examples; SAE latents and steering vectors are model-specific and need retraining per target model; fluency-effectiveness tradeoff—most effective prompts lack semantic coherence. Broader impact: aims to improve LLM safety by suppressing undesired personas but pipeline could enable jailbreak/harmful-output discovery; recommend access controls. Acknowledgment: used Claude (Anthropic) for manuscript writing assistance and AI-assisted code generation.

Paper studies automatic prompt discovery for controlling behavioral personas in LLMs. Introduces RESGA (RESidual Gradient Ascent) using dense residual representations and SAEGA (Sparse Autoencoder Gradient Ascent) using sparse autoencoder features. Both build persona directions from contrasting examples and optimize prompts subject to a fluency constraint. Experiments target sycophancy (agreement with incorrect user opinion), hallucination (evaluated via TruthfulQA error), and myopic reward (short-term reward seeking over long-term outcomes). Reports improvements on Llama 3.1, Qwen 2.5, and Gemma 3. Abstract states a sycophancy improvement of 49.90% compared with 79.24% (numbers noted as presented). Mechanistic analyses claim SAEGA suppresses relevant features, concentrates behavior near neutrality, and preserves natural activation sparsity. Limitations listed: need for labeled data, steering directions that are model-specific, and prompt coherence issues.

Paper studies automatic prompt discovery to steer behavioral personas (sycophancy, hallucination via TruthfulQA, myopic reward) using RESGA (RESidual Gradient Ascent: dense residual steering vector v_repr from mean-representation differences) and SAEGA (Sparse Autoencoder Gradient Ascent: steering via selected SAE encoder directions v_SAE). Persona directions are built from contrast sets D+ (persona-exhibiting) and D- (persona-free). SAE latents a_i(x) use an encoder W_enc, rows w_i, ReLU and bias b_i; top-K latents I_K selected by |\bar a_i^+ - \bar a_i^-|. The persona-reduction objective f(t) is the negative scaled projection of the prompt representation e(t) onto v; combined objective L_\lambda(t)=f(t)+\lambda H (H = self cross-entropy under model m) balances steering and fluency. Evolutionary Prompt Optimization (EPO) optimizes discrete prompts with population M, prompt length n, iterations T, candidate-replacement size k (gradient-guided selection vs random mutation), restarts, and random/seed initialization. Fluency is measured by prompt self cross-entropy; WikiText2 perplexity is reported for language-modeling. Evaluation: sycophancy error rate (undesirable preference; neutralization=50%), instance-wise neutrality = near-zero, low-variance projections attributed to SAEGA; behavioral reversal = beyond neutrality. Models: Llama 3.1 8B, Qwen 2.5 7B, Gemma 3 4B. Baselines include Zero-Shot, Standard Prompt, Dense Steering Vector, Random Direction, Task Loss objective, and ProTeGi (GPT-4o). Mechanistic claims: SAEGA suppresses persona features, preserves natural sparse topology; RESGA often shifts mean projections (distributional shifting). Table references: Avg. in Table 1; literal optimized prompts in Tables 2–3. Abstract reported sycophancy numbers ~49.90% vs 79.24%.

SAE details: encoder W_enc with rows w_i, latents a_i(x)=ReLU(w_i·e(x)+b_i); select top-K latents by |mean_a_i^+ - mean_a_i^-|. Persona-reduction objective f(t) is negative scaled projection of prompt representation e(t) onto v; combined objective L_λ(t)=f(t)+λH adds prompt fluency regularizer H (prompt self cross-entropy under model m). Optimization uses Evolutionary Prompt Optimization (EPO): population M, prompt length n, iterations T, candidate-replacement size k, gradient-guided selection vs random mutation, restarts/seeds. Fluency measured by prompt self cross-entropy; WikiText2 perplexity reported for LM fluency. Evaluations: three personas (sycophancy, TruthfulQA/hallucination, myopic reward) across three model families (Llama 3.1 8B, Qwen 2.5 7B, Gemma 3 4B). Metrics include sycophancy error rate (neutralization = 50%), instance-wise neutrality, and behavioral reversal. Baselines: Zero-Shot, Standard Prompt, Dense Steering Vector, Random Direction, Task Loss objective, ProTeGi (GPT-4o). Mechanistic claims: SAEGA suppresses persona features while preserving sparse topology; RESGA often shifts mean projections (distributional shifting). Abstract reports sycophancy improvement: 49.90% vs 79.24%.

(2025) find SAE persona features and activation-clamping control; SAEs said introduced in Cunningham et al. (2023b); Matryoshka SAE (Bussmann et al., 2025). steps.notes_before: Section 3 (Method) overview: 3 stages—(1) construct persona steering vector (dense or SAE), (2) fluent gradient-ascent optimization, (3) initialize/select prompts on fluency–steering Pareto frontier. Representation steering (eq.1): v_repr = mean_{D+} e(x) - mean_{D-} e(x). SAE steering (eq.2): select top-K latents by |\bar a_i^+ - \bar a_i^-| and form v_SAE = \sum_{i in I_K} w_i*(\bar a_i^+ - \bar a_i^-); latent a_i(x)=ReLU(w_i e(x)+b_i). Persona-reduction objective (eq.3): f(t) = -<e(t),v>/||e(t)|| (maximize to steer away). Fluent objective: inconsistent presentation — figure/text write L_\lambda = f + H (or f + λH), but Equation (4) gives L_\lambda(t) = f(t) - (λ/n) \sum_i H(m(t_{<=i}), t_{i+1}); λ controls tradeoff. EPO (Algorithm 1): population M prompts with fluency weights {λ_i}, iterate T steps, compute L and gradients, select top-k per position by gradient magnitude, mutate by replacing tokens with sampled top-k, evaluate and select best per λ, periodic restarts keep best prompt. Minor self-contradiction: algorithm step says gradients w.r.t. one-hot encodings, later text says gradients w.r.t. token embeddings. Claim: EPO improves Llama myopic-reward error by 23.50 points over random mutation (reported here).

Initialization (part 7): two strategies—random (uniform tokens) and seed (short natural-language phrase). Seed inits claimed to anchor to language manifold and occupy higher-fluency parts of Pareto frontier; fluency measured by model self cross-entropy (discussed via perplexity). steps.notes_before: Methods: Two prompt-discovery methods evaluated: RESGA (residual-based GA) and SAEGA (SAE-based GA). Experiments (Sec.4): tasks—sycophancy, hallucination (TruthfulQA multiple-choice), myopic reward. Results: Table1 per-task entries — Sycophancy: RESGA [49.86,50.63,62.65], SAEGA [49.84,49.95,70.70]; Hallucination: RESGA [45.12,41.46,51.22], SAEGA [46.95,40.85,49.14]; Myopic: RESGA [38.50,38.50,34.50], SAEGA [31.50,40.50,38.50]. Averages: RESGA 45.83, SAEGA 46.44. Baselines: Standard Prompt 55.45, Dense Steering 56.10. Table3 seed→optimized reductions summarized earlier.

Table4 perplexities pre→post: Llama 12.56→12.07 (↓), Qwen 10.88→12.48 (↑), Gemma 30.51→29.19 (↓).

Mechanisms: RESGA sometimes injects alternative-label tokens. SAEGA suppresses agreement tokens and upweights contrast/connective tokens; both methods upweight long-term-planning tokens.

Ablations (Table5): Random Direction / Random Mutation / Task Loss perform worse. Paper asserts persona-direction steering is essential and random mutation degrades; task-loss is unstable. Note: earlier-recorded internal conflict — elsewhere paper says SAEGA "collapses variance" (direction-insensitive), which contradicts the claim that persona-direction steering is essential/ interpretable.

Conclusions/future work: Discovered prompts improve persona metrics; SAEGA 'neutralizes' behavior and preserves natural activation manifolds (~50 active features vs >150 for dense). Proposes lower-data, cross-model, multi-persona future work.

New (Part 14) Limitations: both methods require labeled examples; SAE latents and steering vectors are model-specific and require retraining per target model; fluency-effectiveness tradeoff — most effective prompts lack semantic coherence, suggesting stronger linguistic priors to favor natural-language-like prompts.

errors.claim: "Our framework discovers persona-steering prompts through a three-stage pipeline."

errors.claim: "Figure 2: ... objective $L_{\lambda}(\mathbf{t})=f(\mathbf{t})+H(\mathbf{t})$"

The sign and the presence of the lambda scaling disagree, which changes whether fluency is encouraged or discouraged and is therefore a substantive internal inconsistency.

errors.claim: Seed-initialized prompts consequently occupy higher-fluency regions of the Pareto frontier without significantly sacrificing steering effectiveness, making them preferable when interpretability of the discovered prompt is desired.

errors.claim: The first is random initialization, where prompts are seeded with uniformly sampled vocabulary tokens, which tends to produce syntactically fragmented or semantically incoherent discovered prompts.

Broader impact: warns that pipeline could be adapted to target safety-critical SAE latents (jailbreak discovery/harmful outputs) and recommends access controls. Title/authors: Gradient-ascent based prompt discovery for interpretable persona control — Harshvardhan Saini, Yiming Tang, Dianbo Liu. Methods: RESGA (constructs persona steering vectors from residual-stream / dense representation differences) and SAEGA (uses SAE-discovered latents as interpretable persona features). Both use a "fluent gradient ascent" procedure to discover natural-language prompts with controllable fluency. Tasks/models: steer three personas — sycophancy, hallucination, myopic reward — evaluated on Llama 3.1, Qwen 2.5, Gemma 3. Claims: automatically discovered prompts significantly improve sycophancy and myopic reward versus manual prompting and dense (activation) steering (Sec 4.2); representation-level evidence claimed that prompt-based steering avoids distributional shifts caused by dense steering. Repo: github.com/HarshSaini10/RESGA_SAEGA. Related work summary from this part: persona-steering prior work includes RLHF and Constitutional AI; Representation Engineering (RepE) and Contrastive Activation Addition (CAA) extract/apply concept directions/steering vectors; activation steering shown to mitigate sycophancy/toxicity/bias; Wang et al. (2025) report SAE latents capture persona features usable via activation clamping. SAEs: cited as introduced in Cunningham et al. (2023b); SAEs can reveal monosemantic neurons and reduce superposition; related techniques include JumpReLU, Top-K, Batch Top-K, Matryoshka SAEs; LLM-based analyses and subpopulation inspection often used to interpret SAE neurons. Prompt-engineering context: GPT-3, chain-of-thought, self-consistency, PAL/PoT, evolutionary prompt optimization (EPO), Greedy Coordinate Gradient (GCG), ProTeGi, and theoretical framing viewing prompting as optimal control. Caveats to check later: (1) paper has earlier inconsistent language about optimization objective (maximize vs steer away), (2) abstract sycophancy percentages ambiguous (49.90% vs 79.24%), (3) ensure evidence supports claim that prompt-based steering avoids distributional shifts from dense steering.

steps.notes_before: Paper: RESGA & SAEGA for persona steering. Section 3 overview: pipeline (text says three-stage: 1) construct steering vectors, 2) fluent gradient ascent to discover prompts, 3) initialize/select prompts), but Figure 2 caption describes only two stages (vector construction + optimization) and shows an inconsistent objective form (see errors). Persona steering vectors: Representation-based (Eq.1) v_repr = mean_{D+} e(x) - mean_{D-} e(x). SAE-based (Eq.2): select top-K latents I_K by |mean activation difference|; v_SAE = sum_{i in I_K} w_i * (bar a_i^+ - bar a_i^-), with a_i(x)=ReLU(w_i e(x)+b_i) and w_i row of W_enc. Persona reduction objective: f(t) = - <e(t), v> / ||e(t)|| (Eq.3); text: maximize f to push representations away from persona direction. Fluency-regularized objective: Eq.(4) L_lambda(t) = f(t) - (lambda/n) sum_{i} H(m(prefix), next_token), where H is cross-entropy; note this conflicts with Figure 2's stated L_lambda = f + H. Optimization: use Evolutionary Prompt Optimization (EPO) — population M, fluency weights {lambda_i}, prompt length n, gradient magnitudes to pick top-k token candidates per position, mutate by token replacement, periodic restarts, select best per lambda to span Pareto frontier.

final_notes:
Scope & tasks: Experiments on three tasks — B2R (sophistication/undesired persona), U9K (hallucination; TruthfulQA multiple-choice), D6V (myopic reward). Lower metric = better (fraction preferring undesirable option). Models: C7N = Llama3.1-8B, W4X = Qwen2.5-7B, F9S = Gemma3-4B. Intervention layers: C7N/W4X = 25, F9S = 20. Prompt length n = 8; T = 1000. SAE natural L0 ≈ 50, latent K = 20.

Key quantitative results (reported): QX2 (optimized prompt) B2R per-model = C7N 49.86, W4X 50.63, F9S 62.65. V7P (another prompt) B2R per-model = C7N 49.84, W4X 49.95, F9S 70.70. Ablations (Table 5): K3Y (Random Direction) B2R=[74.13,84.56,81.47], U9K=[68.29,54.26,84.70], D6V=[50.50,48.50,61.00]; E8U (Random Mutation) B2R=[68.00,71.66,76.04], U9K=[50.40,45.12,54.26], D6V=[52.00,46.50,55.00]; M5A B2R=[55.83,73.50,58.70]. QX2 and V7P rows same as above.

Mechanistic/token-level claims: V7P allegedly suppresses tokens like “Yes/True/Agree” and upweights connectors like “However/But” (framing as critical-evaluation priming). QX2 and V7P reportedly upweight long-term/planning tokens on D6V.

Limitations & conclusion (this part): Semi-supervised reduction of labeled-data requirements, cross-model transferability of discovered prompts, and multi-persona steering are cited as future directions. Explicit limitations state: QX2 and V7P require labeled examples to discover prompts; SAE latents and steering vectors are model-specific (require retraining per model); most effective prompts lack semantic coherence (fluency–effectiveness tradeoff). Broader impact warns method could be misused; deployment needs access controls. Acknowledgment notes Claude (Anthropic) assisted manuscript writing and AI-assisted code generation.

Unresolved/internal contradictions to track from earlier parts: (1) Earlier text (previous part) reportedly claims K3Y has lower U9K than E8U, but Table 5 numbers show K3Y U9K is larger (worse) than E8U. (2) Token-level portrayal of V7P as enabling nuance conflicts with earlier notes that V7P caused sharp variance collapse to neutrality and with V7P's poor F9S B2R (70.70). Other unresolved issues from prior parts: Table 3 seed vs optimized phrasing inconsistency; W4X perplexity increase claim.

steps.notes_before: Three-stage method: (i) persona-vector construction, (ii) fluency-constrained discovery, (iii) initialization/frontier selection via validation. Persona vectors: v_repr = (1/|D+|) sum_{x in D+} e(x) - (1/|D-|) sum_{x in D-} e(x) (eq 1). SAE alternative: v_SAE = sum_{i in I_K} w_i * (\bar a_i^+ - \bar a_i^-), with a_i(x)=ReLU(w_i e(x)+b_i) and \bar a^+,\bar a^- means over D^+,D^- (eq 2). Persona-reduction objective: f(t) = -<e(t),v>/||e(t)|| (eq 3) — maximizing f pushes representations away from the persona direction (reduces persona). Fluency control: objective L_λ balances f and next-token cross-entropy H; however the paper gives two inconsistent forms — a caption L_λ = f + H and Eq. (4) L_λ = f - (λ/n) sum_i H(m(t_{≤i}), t_{i+1}) (the latter includes sign and λ/n scaling). Algorithm: N8C (population M, per-candidate λ_i) uses gradients on one-hot token encodings, top-k token selection per position, random-token mutation, periodic restarts, and selects prompts across the fluency–steering Pareto frontier. Initialization: natural-language seeds (e.g., "Please answer honestly" for B2R) bias search toward higher-fluency frontier regions; candidates are appended to validation inputs and selected by downstream behavioral metric. Frontier analysis prefers intermediate prompts balancing steering and moderate perplexity increases; fluency here is self cross-entropy (no hard threshold).

final_notes:
Methods: three-stage persona steering (RESGA, SAEGA). Prompt optimization EPO (M=100, n=8, T=1000). Models: Llama 3.1 8B, Qwen 2.5 7B, Gemma 3 4B. Target layers: Llama/Qwen 25, Gemma 20. SAEGA K=20; natural sparsity L0 ≈ 50.

Table 1 key numbers (per-model triples):
- Zero-Shot sycophancy/hallucination/myopic: [72.48, 86.00, 82.00]; [51.45, 45.00, 57.97]; [54.00, 55.00, 58.00].
- RESGA: syc [49.86, 50.63, 62.65]; hall [45.12, 41.46, 51.22]; myopic [38.50, 38.50, 34.50].
- SAEGA: syc [49.84, 49.95, 70.70]; hall [46.95, 40.85, 49.14]; myopic [31.50, 40.50, 38.50].
Averages: RESGA mean 45.83; SAEGA mean 46.44; Standard Prompt 55.45; Dense Steering Vector 56.10.

Table 5 ablations (triples): Random Direction: [74.13,84.56,81.47]; [68.29,54.26,84.70]; [50.50,48.50,61.00]. Random Mutation: [68.00,71.66,76.04]; [50.40,45.12,54.26]; [52.00,46.50,55.00]. Task Loss: [55.83,73.50,58.70]; [46.95,45.12,54.27]; [48.50,48.00,51.50].

Observed issues to track: (1) "Meaningful persona direction is essential" claim not clearly supported by ablations; (2) "Random mutation consistently degrades performance" is too strong; (3) Task-loss objective not uniformly worse.

Mechanistic claims: SAEGA neutralizes behavior (neutrality ≈ 0.0), preserves activation manifold (baseline ≈50 active features; dense steering >150; SAEGA ≈50–60), selective suppression and stable trajectory geometry.

Limitations: needs labeled persona examples; SAE latents and steering vectors are model-specific; many effective prompts lack semantic coherence (fluency-effectiveness tradeoff).

Broader impact: aims to improve safety by suppressing undesired personas; warns pipeline could be misused to discover jailbreaks/harmful outputs and recommends access controls. Acknowledgment: used Claude (Anthropic) for manuscript writing and AI-assisted code generation.

Paper studies automatic prompt discovery for controlling behavioral personas in LLMs. Introduces RESGA (RESidual Gradient Ascent) using dense residual representations and SAEGA (Sparse Autoencoder Gradient Ascent) using sparse autoencoder features. Both build persona directions from contrasting examples and optimize prompts subject to a fluency constraint. Experiments target sycophancy (agreement with incorrect user opinion), hallucination (evaluated via TruthfulQA error), and myopic reward (short-term reward seeking over long-term outcomes). Reports improvements on Llama 3.1, Qwen 2.5, and Gemma 3. Abstract states a sycophancy improvement of 49.90% compared with 79.24% (numbers noted as presented). Mechanistic analyses claim SAEGA suppresses relevant features, concentrates behavior near neutrality, and preserves natural activation sparsity. Limitations listed: need for labeled data, steering directions that are model-specific, and prompt coherence issues.

Paper studies automatic prompt discovery to steer behavioral personas (sycophancy, hallucination via TruthfulQA, myopic reward) using RESGA (RESidual Gradient Ascent: dense residual steering vector v_repr from mean-representation differences) and SAEGA (Sparse Autoencoder Gradient Ascent: steering via selected SAE encoder directions v_SAE). Persona directions are built from contrast sets D+ (persona-exhibiting) and D- (persona-free). SAE latents a_i(x) use an encoder W_enc, rows w_i, ReLU and bias b_i; top-K latents I_K selected by |\bar a_i^+ - \bar a_i^-|. The persona-reduction objective f(t) is the negative scaled projection of the prompt representation e(t) onto v; combined objective L_\lambda(t)=f(t)+\lambda H (H = self cross-entropy under model m) balances steering and fluency. Evolutionary Prompt Optimization (EPO) optimizes discrete prompts with population M, prompt length n, iterations T, candidate-replacement size k (gradient-guided selection vs random mutation), restarts, and random/seed initialization. Fluency is measured by prompt self cross-entropy; WikiText2 perplexity is reported for language-modeling. Evaluation: sycophancy error rate (undesirable preference; neutralization=50%), instance-wise neutrality = near-zero, low-variance projections attributed to SAEGA; behavioral reversal = beyond neutrality. Models: Llama 3.1 8B, Qwen 2.5 7B, Gemma 3 4B. Baselines include Zero-Shot, Standard Prompt, Dense Steering Vector, Random Direction, Task Loss objective, and ProTeGi (GPT-4o). Mechanistic claims: SAEGA suppresses persona features, preserves natural sparse topology; RESGA often shifts mean projections (distributional shifting). Table references: Avg. in Table 1; literal optimized prompts in Tables 2–3. Abstract reported sycophancy numbers ~49.90% vs 79.24%.

SAE details: encoder W_enc with rows w_i, latents a_i(x)=ReLU(w_i·e(x)+b_i); select top-K latents by |mean_a_i^+ - mean_a_i^-|. Optimization uses Evolutionary Prompt Optimization (EPO): population M, prompt length n, iterations T, candidate-replacement size k, gradient-guided selection vs random mutation, restarts/seeds. Mechanistic claims: SAEGA suppresses persona features while preserving sparse topology; RESGA often shifts mean projections (distributional shifting). Abstract reports sycophancy improvement: 49.90% vs 79.24%.

steps.notes_before: Methods (Section 3) — three-stage framework (text claims 3 stages though Figure 2 calls it 2-stage): (1) construct persona steering vector v either via representation-difference (Eq.1: v_repr = mean_{D+} e(x) - mean_{D-} e(x)) or via SAE latents (select top-K latents by |bar a_i^+ - bar a_i^-|; Eq.2: v_SAE = sum_{i in I_K} w_i * (bar a_i^+ - bar a_i^-); a_i(x)=ReLU(w_i e(x)+b_i)). Output: diverse prompts spanning fluency–steering frontier.

final_notes: Models/tasks: Llama, Qwen, Gemma; persona tasks: Sycophancy, Hallucination, Myopic Reward. Key method results: RESGA — Sycophancy: 49.86, 50.63, 62.65; Hallucination: 45.12, 41.46, 51.22; Myopic: 38.50, 38.50, 34.50 (avg ≈45.83). SAEGA — Sycophancy: 49.84, 49.95, 70.70; Hallucination: 46.95, 40.85, 49.14; Myopic: 31.50, 40.50, 38.50 (avg ≈46.44). Ablations (Table 5): Random Direction (Syc:74.13,84.56,81.47; Halluc:68.29,54.26,84.70; Myopic:50.50,48.50,61.00), Random Mutation (Syc:68.00,71.66,76.04; Halluc:50.40,45.12,54.26; Myopic:52.00,46.50,55.00), Task Loss as Objective (Syc:55.83,73.50,58.70; Halluc:46.95,45.12,54.27; Myopic:48.50,48.00,51.50). Note: Task Loss sometimes outperforms SAEGA (e.g., Gemma Sycophancy). Mechanistic claims: RESGA often token-primes; SAEGA claimed to perform semantic steering and enforce instance-wise neutrality. Perplexity (WikiText2): Llama 12.56→12.07, Qwen 10.88→12.48, Gemma 30.51→29.19 (paper described these changes as negligible despite Qwen's notable increase). Limitations (from last part): (1) methods require labeled examples with and without target persona; (2) SAE latents/steering vectors are model-specific and require retraining per target model; (3) fluency-effectiveness tradeoff — most effective prompts lack semantic coherence, conflicting with earlier 'interpretable control' claim. Broader impact (this part): authors note dual-use risk — pipeline could be adapted to target safety-critical SAE latents enabling jailbreaks/harmful outputs; recommend access controls. Acknowledgment: used Claude (Anthropic) for manuscript writing assistance and AI-assisted code generation.

Title/authors: Gradient-ascent based prompt discovery for interpretable persona control — Harshvardhan Saini, Yiming Tang, Dianbo Liu. Methods: RESGA (constructs persona steering vectors from residual-stream / dense representation differences) and SAEGA (uses SAE-discovered latents as interpretable persona features). Both use a "fluent gradient ascent" procedure to discover natural-language prompts with controllable fluency. Tasks/models: steer three personas — sycophancy, hallucination, myopic reward — evaluated on Llama 3.1, Qwen 2.5, Gemma 3. Claims: automatically discovered prompts significantly improve sycophancy and myopic reward versus manual prompting and dense (activation) steering (Sec 4.2); representation-level evidence claimed that prompt-based steering avoids distributional shifts caused by dense steering. Repo: github.com/HarshSaini10/RESGA_SAEGA. Related work summary from this part: persona-steering prior work includes RLHF and Constitutional AI; Representation Engineering (RepE) and Contrastive Activation Addition (CAA) extract/apply concept directions/steering vectors; activation steering shown to mitigate sycophancy/toxicity/bias; Wang et al. (2025) report SAE latents capture persona features usable via activation clamping. SAEs: cited as introduced in Cunningham et al. (2023b); SAEs can reveal monosemantic neurons and reduce superposition; related techniques include JumpReLU, Top-K, Batch Top-K, Matryoshka SAEs; LLM-based analyses and subpopulation inspection often used to interpret SAE neurons. Prompt-engineering context: GPT-3, chain-of-thought, self-consistency, PAL/PoT, evolutionary prompt optimization (EPO), Greedy Coordinate Gradient (GCG), ProTeGi, and theoretical framing viewing prompting as optimal control. Caveats to check later: (1) paper has earlier inconsistent language about optimization objective (maximize vs steer away), (2) abstract sycophancy percentages ambiguous (49.90% vs 79.24%), (3) ensure evidence supports claim that prompt-based steering avoids distributional shifts from dense steering.

steps.notes_before: Paper: RESGA & SAEGA for persona steering. Section 3 overview: pipeline (text says three-stage: 1) construct steering vectors, 2) fluent gradient ascent to discover prompts, 3) initialize/select prompts), but Figure 2 caption describes only two stages (vector construction + optimization) and shows an inconsistent objective form (see errors). Persona steering vectors: Representation-based (Eq.1) v_repr = mean_{D+} e(x) - mean_{D-} e(x). SAE-based (Eq.2): select top-K latents I_K by |mean activation difference|; v_SAE = sum_{i in I_K} w_i * (bar a_i^+ - bar a_i^-), with a_i(x)=ReLU(w_i e(x)+b_i) and w_i row of W_enc. Persona reduction objective: f(t) = - <e(t), v> / ||e(t)|| (Eq.3); text: maximize f to push representations away from persona direction. Fluency-regularized objective: Eq.(4) L_lambda(t) = f(t) - (lambda/n) sum_{i} H(m(prefix), next_token), where H is cross-entropy; note this conflicts with Figure 2's stated L_lambda = f + H. Optimization: use Evolutionary Prompt Optimization (EPO) — population M, fluency weights {lambda_i}, prompt length n, gradient magnitudes to pick top-k token candidates per position, mutate by token replacement, periodic restarts, select best per lambda to span Pareto frontier.

errors.claim: Seed-initialized prompts consequently occupy higher-fluency regions of the Pareto frontier without significantly sacrificing steering effectiveness, making them preferable when interpretability of the discovered prompt is desired.

errors.claim: The first is random initialization, where prompts are seeded with uniformly sampled vocabulary tokens, which tends to produce syntactically fragmented or semantically incoherent discovered prompts.

final_notes:
Tasks: B2R (sycophancy/polite disagreement), U9K (TruthfulQA MC), D6V (myopic reward). Lower is better.

Models: C7N = Llama3.1-8B, W4X = Qwen2.5-7B, F9S = Gemma3-4B. V7P uses SAE (SAELens) autoencoders; SAE L0 ≈ 50; intervention layers: C7N/W4X = 25, F9S = 20.

Key results (from earlier tables): QX2 B2R: C7N 49.86, W4X 50.63, F9S 62.65. V7P B2R: C7N 49.84, W4X 49.95, F9S 70.70.

Lexical priming: V7P reportedly suppresses tokens like "Yes/True/Agree" and upweights "However/But" (critical-evaluation priming). For D6V, QX2 and V7P upweight long-term vocabulary ("Future/Long/Wait").

Ablations (Table 5) — entries per model order (C7N, W4X, F9S):
K3Y: B2R [74.13,84.56,81.47], U9K [68.29,54.26,84.70], D6V [50.50,48.50,61.00].
E8U: B2R [68.00,71.66,76.04], U9K [50.40,45.12,54.26], D6V [52.00,46.50,55.00].
M5A: B2R [55.83,73.50,58.70], U9K [46.95,45.12,54.27], D6V [48.50,48.00,51.50].
QX2 baseline: B2R [49.86,50.63,62.65], U9K [45.12,41.46,51.22], D6V [38.50,38.50,34.50].
V7P: B2R [49.84,49.95,70.70], U9K [46.95,40.85,49.14], D6V [31.50,40.50,38.50].

Contradictions flagged earlier to track: (1) Table3 seed vs optimized prompt claim mismatch (optimized prompts show lower scores despite text claiming seeds produce lower error). (2) Table4 perplexity claim mismatch (text said negligible change but W4X perplexity increases notably).

Final part (this submission): Conclusion lists future directions: semi-supervised labeled-data reduction, cross-model transferability, multi-persona steering. Limitations: labeled examples required; SAE latents and steering vectors are model-specific (retraining needed); fluency–effectiveness tradeoff (most effective prompts lack semantic coherence). Broader impact: could aid safety or be misused. Acknowledgment: Claude assisted.

steps.notes_before: Three-stage method: (i) persona-vector construction, (ii) fluency-constrained discovery, (iii) initialization/frontier selection via validation. Persona vectors: v_repr = (1/|D+|) sum_{x in D+} e(x) - (1/|D-|) sum_{x in D-} e(x) (eq 1). SAE alternative: v_SAE = sum_{i in I_K} w_i * (\bar a_i^+ - \bar a_i^-), with a_i(x)=ReLU(w_i e(x)+b_i) and \bar a^+,\bar a^- means over D^+,D^- (eq 2). Persona-reduction objective: f(t) = -<e(t),v>/||e(t)|| (eq 3) — maximizing f pushes representations away from the persona direction (reduces persona). Fluency control: objective L_λ balances f and next-token cross-entropy H; however the paper gives two inconsistent forms — a caption L_λ = f + H and Eq. (4) L_λ = f - (λ/n) sum_i H(m(t_{≤i}), t_{i+1}) (the latter includes sign and λ/n scaling). Algorithm: N8C (population M, per-candidate λ_i) uses gradients on one-hot token encodings, top-k token selection per position, random-token mutation, periodic restarts, and selects prompts across the fluency–steering Pareto frontier. Initialization: natural-language seeds (e.g., "Please answer honestly" for B2R) bias search toward higher-fluency frontier regions; candidates are appended to validation inputs and selected by downstream behavioral metric. Frontier analysis prefers intermediate prompts balancing steering and moderate perplexity increases; fluency here is self cross-entropy (no hard threshold).

SAEGA cells: sycophancy 49.84/49.95/70.70; hallucination 46.95/40.85/49.14; myopic reward 31.50/40.50/38.50. Reported averages: RESGA 45.83, SAEGA 46.44, Standard Prompt 55.45, Dense Steering Vector 56.10 (RESGA/SAEGA outperform Standard & Dense on avg). Main findings: discovered prompts significantly reduce sycophancy and myopic-reward preferences and consistently improve hallucination; RESGA slightly better on average but SAEGA shows model/task variability (e.g., Gemma sycophancy). Mechanistic claims: SAEGA “neutralizes” behavior (neutrality ≈ 0.0) while preserving natural activation manifolds; active-feature counts: baseline ≈50, dense steering >150, SAEGA ≈50–60; selective suppression (Fig.5) and stable trajectory geometry (Fig.6). Ablations (Table 5): Random Direction ≈ zero-shot for sycophancy but worse for hallucination; Random Mutation/Task Loss worse than RESGA/SAEGA. Limitations: requires labeled examples (supervision), SAE latents and steering vectors are model-specific (need retraining per model), fluency-effectiveness tradeoff (most effective discovered prompts lack semantic coherence). Broader impact: aims to improve LLM safety by suppressing undesired personas but the same pipeline could, in principle, be used to target safety-critical SAE latents and automate jailbreak/harmful-output discovery — deployment should include access controls. Acknowledgment: authors report using Claude (Anthropic) for manuscript writing assistance and AI-assisted code generation.

Evaluation: sycophancy error rate (undesirable preference; neutralization=50%), instance-wise neutrality = near-zero, low-variance projections attributed to SAEGA; behavioral reversal = beyond neutrality. Optimization: Evolutionary Prompt Optimization (EPO) with population M, length n, iterations T, replacement k, gradient-guided replacement vs random mutation, restarts/seeds. Evaluation: three personas — sycophancy, hallucination (TruthfulQA), myopic reward — across three model families (Llama 3.1 8B, Qwen 2.5 7B, Gemma 3 4B). Metrics: sycophancy error rate (neutralization = 50%), instance-wise neutrality, behavioral reversal. Baselines: Zero-Shot, Standard Prompt, Dense Steering Vector, Random Direction, Task Loss objective, ProTeGi (GPT-4o). (2025) find SAE persona features and activation-clamping control; SAEs said introduced in Cunningham et al. (2023b); Matryoshka SAE (Bussmann et al., 2025). steps.notes_before: Methods (Section 3) — three-stage framework (text claims 3 stages though Figure 2 calls it 2-stage): (1) construct persona steering vector v either via representation-difference (Eq.1: v_repr = mean_{D+} e(x) - mean_{D-} e(x)) or via SAE latents (select top-K latents by |bar a_i^+ - bar a_i^-|; Eq.2: v_SAE = sum_{i in I_K} w_i * (bar a_i^+ - bar a_i^-); a_i(x)=ReLU(w_i e(x)+b_i)). (2) Fluent gradient-ascent prompt search optimizing persona-reduction f(t) and fluency. f(t) = -<e(t),v>/||e(t)|| where e(t) is last-token representation (Eq.3). Formal objective given as Eq.4: L_λ(t) = f(t) - (λ/n) sum_{i=0}^{n-1} H(m(t_{<=i}), t_{i+1}) (λ trades off fluency; H is cross-entropy penalizing low-probability tokens). EPO algorithm: population M with per-prompt fluency weights {λ_i}; initialize M prompts length n; iterate T times: compute L_{λ_i} and gradients w.r.t. one-hot encodings, pick top-k candidate tokens per position by gradient magnitude, mutate by replacing a random token with sampled top-k alternatives, evaluate and keep best per λ_i; periodic restarts retain one best and reinit others. Output: diverse prompts spanning fluency–steering frontier.

final_notes:
Key reported metrics (assumed order Llama, Qwen, Gemma):
- RESGA sycophancy: 49.86, 50.63, 62.65; hallucination: 45.12, 41.46, 51.22; myopic: 38.50, 38.50, 34.50.
- SAEGA sycophancy: 49.84, 49.95, 70.70; hallucination: 46.95, 40.85, 49.14; myopic: 31.50, 40.50, 38.50.
Other highlights/claims:
- Discovered prompts reportedly yield significant improvements on sycophancy and myopic reward, consistent hallucination improvements, and outperform manual/dense steering.
- SAEGA is claimed to "neutralize rather than shift" behavior and to "preserve natural activation manifolds" via interpretable feature-level control.
Selected table data:
- Table 4 (perplexity, WikiText2): Llama 12.56→12.07, Qwen 10.88→12.48, Gemma 30.51→29.19.
- Table 3 examples: seeds often higher (worse) than optimized, e.g., 71.15→54.22; 72.06→51.72.
- Ablations (Table 5) Random Direction sycophancy: 74.13, 84.56, 81.47; Task Loss sycophancy: 55.83, 73.50, 58.70.
Persisting internal inconsistency: SAEGA's "neutralize/collapse variance" claim conflicts with reported high sycophancy for some models (RESGA 62.65; SAEGA 70.70) and with separate statements about preserving activation manifolds.
New limitations (part 11): requires labeled examples with/without target persona; SAE latents and steering vectors are model-specific and need retraining per target model; most effective prompts lack semantic coherence (fluency–effectiveness tradeoff). Broader impact: could be adapted to automate jailbreaks; deploy with access controls. Acknowledgment: used Claude for manuscript writing and AI-assisted code generation.

steps.notes_before: Title/authors as before. Methods: RESGA (representation-based steering) and SAEGA (SAE latent-based steering). Pipeline: (1) Construct steering vector v in R^d either via representation differences v_repr = mean_{x in D+} e(x) - mean_{x in D-} e(x), or via SAEs: identify top-K latents I_K by contrastive activation and set v_SAE = sum_{i in I_K} w_i * (bar_a_i^+ - bar_a_i^-), where a_i(x)=ReLU(w_i e(x)+b_i). (2) Fluent Gradient Ascent: persona-reduction objective f(t) = -<e(t), v>/||e(t)|| (maximize to make prompt representation point away from persona). Full-objective inconsistency: Figure 2 writes L_lambda(t)=f(t)+H(t), but Eq. (4) gives L_lambda(t)=f(t) - (lambda/n) sum_{i=0}^{n-1} H(m(prefix), next_token), with H the cross-entropy and lambda controlling fluency tradeoff. (3) Optimization via Evolutionary Prompt Optimization (EPO): population M, prompt length n, per-lambda weights {lambda_1..lambda_M}, select top-k tokens per position by gradient magnitude, mutate by sampling replacements, periodic restarts, and select Pareto-front prompts (Sec 3.3 to follow). Note: Algorithm 1 says gradients w.r.t. one-hot token encodings while the text says gradients w.r.t. token embeddings — inconsistent.

Methods: Two steering vector constructions: RESGA (representation-based) v_repr = mean_{x in D+} e(x) - mean_{x in D-} e(x); SAEGA (SAE-latent) identify top-K latents I_K by contrastive activation, v_SAE = sum_{i in I_K} w_i*(bar_a_i^+ - bar_a_i^-), with a_i(x)=ReLU(w_i e(x)+b_i). Optimization: Fluent Gradient Ascent uses persona-reduction objective f(t) = -<e(t), v>/||e(t)|| (maximize to reduce persona). Full-objective inconsistency noted: Figure 2 writes L_lambda(t)=f(t)+H(t) whereas Eq. (4) defines L_lambda(t)=f(t) - (lambda/n) sum_{i=0}^{n-1} H(m(prefix), next_token) (H is cross-entropy; lambda trades fluency). EPO (Evolutionary Prompt Optimization): population M with per-lambda weights, select top-k tokens per position by gradient magnitude, mutate by sampling replacements, periodic restarts, select Pareto-front prompts; note inconsistency: Algorithm 1 uses gradients w.r.t. one-hot token encodings while text refers to gradients w.r.t. token embeddings. New (Part 5): EPO initialization: random (uniform vocab tokens → fragmented/incoherent prompts) or seed (short natural-language phrase related to persona, e.g., “Please answer honestly” → anchors to language manifold). EPO yields prompts spanning Pareto frontier between steering strength and model fluency. Evaluate on held-out validation by appending prompts and measuring change in behavioral metric. Fluency measured as prompt self cross-entropy under the LM (lower = closer to training distribution). No hard fluency threshold; report full Pareto frontier and emphasize intermediate-region prompts balancing steering with moderate perplexity increases vs random-token baselines. Also measure prompt stability across diverse validation examples. Primary goal: causal steering efficacy over linguistic naturalness.

steps.notes_before: Three-stage method: (1) persona-vector construction, (2) fluency-constrained prompt discovery, (3) initialization/frontier selection by validation. Persona steering vectors: direct representation difference v_repr = mean_{x in D+} e(x) - mean_{x in D-} e(x) (Eq. 1). SAE-based V7P: v_SAE = sum_{i in I_K} w_i * (\bar a_i^+ - \bar a_i^-) where \bar a_i^{\pm} are mean ReLU activations a_i(x)=ReLU(w_i e(x)+b_i), and w_i is row i of W_enc (Eq. 2). Suppression target is direction v in R^d; e(x) is activation at chosen layer. Prompt discovery (J4Z) uses gradient-guided evolutionary search (Algorithm N8C): maintain M candidate length-n prompts with fluency weights {\lambda_i}, compute gradients w.r.t. one-hot encodings, pick top-k token candidates per position, mutate by replacing random tokens, evaluate and keep best per \lambda, with periodic restarts. Persona-reduction objective: f(t)= -<e(t),v>/||e(t)|| (Eq. 3); maximizing f reduces alignment with v. Fluency-regularized objective is given in Eq. (4) as L_{\lambda}(t)= f(t) - (\lambda/n) sum_i H(m(t_{\le i}), t_{i+1}) (penalizes low-probability tokens; \lambda trades steering vs fluency). Initialization: natural-language seeds (e.g., "Please answer honestly") bias search toward higher-fluency frontier; selection uses downstream validation metrics and stability across examples. Note: the text earlier states L=f+H (conflicting with Eq. 4).

final_notes: Models: Llama 3.1 (8B), Qwen 2.5 (7B), Gemma 3 (4B). Tasks: Sycophancy, Hallucination (TruthfulQA), Myopic Reward. Metric: fraction preferring undesirable option (lower is better). Key results: Table-1 averages — RESGA 45.83, SAEGA 46.44, Standard Prompt 55.45, Dense Steering 56.10. Table-5 examples: RESGA per-model triples include values like 49.86|50.63|62.65; SAEGA examples include e.g. 49.84|49.95|70.70 (Gemma sycophancy 70.70 — notable failure). Ablations/zero-shot: Random Direction and Zero-Shot often much worse on Hallucination (Random Dir ~84.56, Zero-Shot ~86.00; Gemma Hallucination ~84.70 vs ~57.97 in another setting). Observed tensions: SAEGA is claimed to 'neutralize' and 'suppress agreement markers' but shows high sycophancy on Gemma and Qwen perplexity can rise (reported 10.88 → 12.48) for some interventions. Limitations: RESGA/SAEGA need labeled examples showing presence/absence of persona; SAE latents/steering vectors are model-specific and require retraining per model; most-effective discovered prompts often lack semantic/linguistic coherence (fluency-effectiveness tradeoff). Future work: lower-data methods, cross-model transfer, multi-persona steering. Broader impacts: authors note potential misuse (automated jailbreak/harmful-output elicitation via the same pipeline) and recommend access controls. Acknowledgment: authors report using Claude (Anthropic) for manuscript writing assistance and AI-assisted code generation.

Paper studies automatic prompt discovery for controlling behavioral personas in LLMs. Introduces RESGA (RESidual Gradient Ascent) using dense residual representations and SAEGA (Sparse Autoencoder Gradient Ascent) using sparse autoencoder features. Both build persona directions from contrasting examples and optimize prompts subject to a fluency constraint. Experiments target sycophancy (agreement with incorrect user opinion), hallucination (evaluated via TruthfulQA error), and myopic reward (short-term reward seeking over long-term outcomes). Reports improvements on Llama 3.1, Qwen 2.5, and Gemma 3. Abstract states a sycophancy improvement of 49.90% compared with 79.24% (numbers noted as presented). Mechanistic analyses claim SAEGA suppresses relevant features, concentrates behavior near neutrality, and preserves natural activation sparsity. Limitations listed: need for labeled data, steering directions that are model-specific, and prompt coherence issues.

Paper studies automatic prompt discovery to steer behavioral personas (sycophancy, hallucination via TruthfulQA, myopic reward) using RESGA (RESidual Gradient Ascent: dense residual steering vector v_repr from mean-representation differences) and SAEGA (Sparse Autoencoder Gradient Ascent: steering via selected SAE encoder directions v_SAE). Persona directions are built from contrast sets D+ (persona-exhibiting) and D- (persona-free). SAE latents a_i(x) use an encoder W_enc, rows w_i, ReLU and bias b_i; top-K latents I_K selected by |\bar a_i^+ - \bar a_i^-|. The persona-reduction objective f(t) is the negative scaled projection of the prompt representation e(t) onto v; combined objective L_\lambda(t)=f(t)+\lambda H (H = self cross-entropy under model m) balances steering and fluency. Evolutionary Prompt Optimization (EPO) optimizes discrete prompts with population M, prompt length n, iterations T, candidate-replacement size k (gradient-guided selection vs random mutation), restarts, and random/seed initialization. Fluency is measured by prompt self cross-entropy; WikiText2 perplexity is reported for language-modeling. Evaluation: sycophancy error rate (undesirable preference; neutralization=50%), instance-wise neutrality = near-zero, low-variance projections attributed to SAEGA; behavioral reversal = beyond neutrality. Models: Llama 3.1 8B, Qwen 2.5 7B, Gemma 3 4B. Baselines include Zero-Shot, Standard Prompt, Dense Steering Vector, Random Direction, Task Loss objective, and ProTeGi (GPT-4o). Mechanistic claims: SAEGA suppresses persona features, preserves natural sparse topology; RESGA often shifts mean projections (distributional shifting). Table references: Avg. in Table 1; literal optimized prompts in Tables 2–3. Abstract reported sycophancy numbers ~49.90% vs 79.24%.

Paper proposes two representation-guided prompt-search methods: RESGA (RESidual Gradient Ascent) using dense residual representations (persona direction v from mean-representation differences between D+ and D-) and SAEGA (Sparse Autoencoder Gradient Ascent) using sparse-autoencoder encoder directions v_SAE. SAE details: encoder W_enc with rows w_i, latents a_i(x)=ReLU(w_i·e(x)+b_i); select top-K latents by |mean_a_i^+ - mean_a_i^-|. Persona-reduction objective f(t) is negative scaled projection of prompt representation e(t) onto v; combined objective L_λ(t)=f(t)+λH adds prompt fluency regularizer H (prompt self cross-entropy under model m). Optimization uses Evolutionary Prompt Optimization (EPO): population M, prompt length n, iterations T, candidate-replacement size k, gradient-guided selection vs random mutation, restarts/seeds. Fluency measured by prompt self cross-entropy; WikiText2 perplexity reported for LM fluency. Evaluations: three personas (sycophancy, TruthfulQA/hallucination, myopic reward) across three model families (Llama 3.1 8B, Qwen 2.5 7B, Gemma 3 4B). Metrics include sycophancy error rate (neutralization = 50%), instance-wise neutrality, and behavioral reversal. Baselines: Zero-Shot, Standard Prompt, Dense Steering Vector, Random Direction, Task Loss objective, ProTeGi (GPT-4o). Mechanistic claims: SAEGA suppresses persona features while preserving sparse topology; RESGA often shifts mean projections (distributional shifting). Abstract reports sycophancy improvement: 49.90% vs 79.24%.
