Title: IA2: Alignment with ICL Activations — Improves Supervised Fine-Tuning. Authors: Aayush Mishra; Daniel Khashabi & Anqi Liu. Introduction claims: SFT (often via PEFT) needs large labeled datasets; ICL generalizes well in few-shot and yields better calibration but costs context/inference compute. Authors report ICL and SFT produce disparate internal activations (§3) even when token-level behavior looks similar. Hypothesis: ICL activations contain richer information for generalization; SFT (especially few-shot) may lack this and overfit/learn shortcuts. They propose IA2 (ICL Activation Alignment), a self-distillation/priming method: (1) collect ICL activations, (2) enforce functional alignment with ICL, then (3) perform SFT on the primed model (§4). Claim IA2 priming before SFT “drastically improves” accuracy and calibration on a variety of text classification and generation tasks (§5). They state they trained >13,000 models across 12 benchmarks to validate results. Also claim the IA2 training signal is absent in SFT-only training. Figure 1 summarizes pipeline and aggregated performance charts. Items to verify in later parts: evidence for distinct activations (§3) (metrics/visualizations); precise IA2 method (which activations/layers, loss, optimization, priming procedure) and compute cost; experimental details and results (§5): datasets, models (note: abstract mentioned two model families), baselines, metrics (accuracy, calibration), statistical significance, and any claims about inference/compute tradeoffs.

Paper: IA2: Alignment with ICL Activations — Improves Supervised Fine-Tuning. Core claim: ICL and SFT produce disparate internal activations even when token-level behavior looks similar; authors propose IA2 (ICL Activation Alignment): collect ICL activations, enforce functional alignment with ICL, then perform SFT on the primed model. They claim IA2 improves accuracy and calibration, trained >13,000 models across 12 benchmarks. 

Section 2 (background/notation) details: decoder-only transformer M_Θ with R token vectors T=[t_i]_{i=1..R}. Self-attention uses weights W_Q,W_K,W_V,W_O (denoted W_QKVO). For causal attention q_i = t_i W_Q, K = t_:i W_K, V = t_:i W_V, and SA output Z = [z_i = softmax(q_i K^T / sqrt(d)) V · W_O]_{i=1..R}. 

SFT: given dataset D_T={(X_i,Y_i)}_{i=1..N}, fine-tune Θ→Θ' by generating G tokens per response and minimizing L_SFT = sum_{i=1..N} sum_{j=1..G} cross-entropy(\bar{Y}_{ij},Y_{ij}). 

ICL: prompt with concatenated demos I=[X1◦Y1◦...◦Xn◦Yn] and query X_t, produce M_Θ(I◦X_t)=\hat{y}_t (classic demo-based ICL). 

Activations: hidden SA outputs form tensor A of shape L×R×d. Activation similarity asim(A1,A2) is token-wise cosine similarity, producing an L×R map.

Section 3 investigates whether ICL and SFT produce similar internal activations. Experiment: collected ICL activations A_ICL (T=[I◦X]) for 100 test samples across datasets (SST2, AGNews, etc.) and models (Qwen3 & Llama-3.2 family: 1B↔16 layers, 3B↔28 layers, 4B↔36 layers). Trained SFT models using the same ICL demos until convergence and collected A_SFT (T=X). Computed asim(A_ICL,A_SFT) at output-token positions (token-wise cosine similarity per §2) and averaged across tokens, samples, datasets (plotted in Figure 2; SFT-only in first row). Result: ICL and SFT activations are not aligned across models — better alignment near initial and final layers, misalignment in middle layers. They note ICL is much better calibrated than SFT at similar (slightly better) accuracy (Figure 1), hypothesizing SFT learns output-oriented shortcuts while ICL uses generalizable circuits. Conclusion: SFT is not a drop-in replacement for ICL; research question: can ICL activations be used to improve SFT (motivating IA2→SFT pipeline described next).

final_notes: Models & setup: Qwen3-4B-Base primary; LoRA rank=8 on self-attention. Metrics: single-token (first-token) accuracy & ECE; multi-token accuracy (GSM8K/GSM8Ks capped at 200 tokens, HMathA capped at 400). Key results (N=4, trained on ground-truth responses, Table 2): GSM8K — w/o 56.4, ICL 76.4, SFT 70.9, IA2→SFT 73.6; GSM8Ks — w/o 45.4, ICL 68.4, SFT 64.5, IA2→SFT 68.8; HMathA — w/o 21.0, ICL 60.4, SFT 50.4, IA2→SFT 55.3; SciQ — w/o 15.4, ICL 37.5, SFT 35.0, IA2→SFT 40.8. Trained on ICL-generated responses (Table 3, N=4): GSM8K: SFT 66.4, IA2→SFT 67.2, IA2+SFT 77.0; GSM8Ks: SFT 59.8, IA2→SFT 61.6, IA2+SFT 69.0; HMathA: SFT 49.0, IA2→SFT 54.0, IA2+SFT 53.6; SciQ: SFT 27.2, IA2→SFT 32.8, IA2+SFT 34.5. Shot-evolution (Table 5): GSM8K ICL N=2 81.2, N=4 76.4, N=8 77.2; IA2→SFT outperforms SFT-only with gaps +9.4, +2.7, +2.5 (ICL sometimes > IA2→SFT, esp. N=2). HMathA shows similar patterns. IA3 experiments (Llama-3.2, Table 6 N=4): IA2→SFT improves over SFT and can exceed ICL. Analyses: SVD overlap indicates SFT updates largely orthogonal to IA2; KD/soft-label baselines (LLaMA 1B) raised multi-token accuracy but worsened single-token calibration. IA2 requires one-time collection of ICL activations; inference cost equals SFT. Ablations/suggestions: LoRA rank/target modules, selective IA2 per-layer, prompt/demo-order optimization, finer-grained LR control. Main conclusions: ICL and SFT adapt via different mechanisms; ICL often encodes richer/generalizable patterns; IA2 induces ICL-like internal behavior and shifts models into a more adaptable weight subspace inaccessible to SFT alone, consistently improving SFT accuracy (paper also claims calibration improvements). Reproducibility: authors state code on GitHub, full details in paper/appendix/README, repeatable random seeds. Acknowledgments: ONR, Amazon Research Award, Open Philanthropy; thanks to Andrea Wynn.

Title: IA2: Alignment with ICL Activations Improves Supervised Fine-Tuning. Authors: Aayush Mishra; Daniel Khashabi & Anqi Liu (Johns Hopkins Univ.). Abstract claims: ICL (in-context learning) adapts at inference and can yield better generalizability and calibration than SFT in data-scarce settings but costs more inference compute. The authors show ICL and SFT produce distinct activation patterns, motivating IA2 (ICL Activation Alignment), a self-distillation technique that trains SFT models to replicate ICL activation patterns and thus encourage ICL-like internal reasoning. IA2 is applied as a priming step before SFT and is reported to significantly improve accuracy and calibration across 12 benchmarks and two model families. Claim also frames this as offering insight into internal mechanics of model adaptation. Correspondence emails given; equal advising footnote noted.

Paper: IA2: Alignment with ICL Activations Improves Supervised Fine-Tuning. Authors: Aayush Mishra; Daniel Khashabi & Anqi Liu. Core problem: SFT (often via PEFT) requires many labeled examples and may overfit/shortcut in few-shot settings; ICL adapts at inference, generalizes well in few-shot and yields better calibration but uses costly context/inference compute. Key observation (§3): ICL and SFT (with the same data) produce disparate internal activations — a functional gap despite similar token-level behavior. Proposal (§4): IA2 (ICL Activation Alignment) — a self-distillation/priming step that (1) collects activations from the model performing ICL, (2) trains the model to align its internal activations to those ICL activations, then (3) performs SFT on this primed model. Contrast to prior work: earlier context-distillation methods use only output/response supervision and may not capture ICL’s internal functional behavior. Claims/results (to be validated in §5): IA2 priming drastically improves SFT performance and calibration across benchmarks; IA2 training signal is absent in SFT-only training. Experimental scale: "over 13,000 models spanning 12 benchmarks" (and earlier note: improvements reported across 12 benchmarks and two model families). Figures: overview in Fig.1; detailed experiments in §5.

Paper: IA2: Alignment with ICL Activations Improves Supervised Fine-Tuning. Background/notation: Decoder-only transformer M_Θ with L layers processes token sequence T=[t_i]_{i=1..R}. Standard self-attention (SA) uses weights W_Q,W_K,W_V,W_O (denoted W_{QKVO}). For position i: q_i = t_i·W_Q, K = t_{:i}·W_K, V = t_{:i}·W_V, and z_i = softmax(q_i K^T / sqrt(d)) V · W_O. SA outputs Z have shape R×d. The paper studies effects of changing context T or weights W_{QKVO}. Supervised fine-tuning (SFT): given D_T = {(X_i,Y_i)}_{i=1..N}, fine-tune Θ→Θ' to produce responses; generate G tokens per ground-truth response Y_i and minimize L_SFT = sum_{i=1}^N sum_{j=1}^G cross-entropy(Ȳ_{ij}, Y_{ij}). In-context learning (ICL): prompt M_Θ with demonstrations I = [X_1 ∘ Y_1 ∘ ... ∘ X_n ∘ Y_n] plus X_t to get response M_Θ(I ∘ X_t)=ĤY_t (no weight updates). Activations: hidden SA outputs are activations A of size L×R×d (layers×tokens×dim). They analyze sequences T=[I ∘ X] for ICL and T=X without ICL under different weights. Define activation similarity asim(A1,A2) as token-wise cosine similarity across d, yielding a matrix of size L×R. Key earlier claims (from notes): §3 observes ICL and SFT produce disparate internal activations; IA2 aligns activations from ICL then SFT to improve performance.

Paper: IA2: Alignment with ICL Activations Improves Supervised Fine-Tuning. Setup: decoder-only transformer M_Θ, SA produces hidden activations A of shape L×R×d. asim(A1,A2) = token-wise cosine similarity across d producing L×R matrix. SFT: fine-tune model on (X,Y) pairs (loss = CE over response tokens). ICL: place demonstrations I = [X1∘Y1...Xn∘Yn] in context and run model without weight updates. Earlier claim: ICL and SFT produce disparate internal activations; aligning SFT activations to ICL (IA2→SFT) improves performance. Current (§3) details: computed A_ICL (T=[I∘X]) and A_SFT (after training SFT on same demos until convergence, then evaluating with T=X) for 100 test samples across datasets (SST2, AGNews, etc.) and models (Qwen3, Llama-3.2 families) and sizes (1B/16L, 3B/28L, 4B/36L). Calculated asim(A_ICL,A_SFT) at output token positions, averaged over tokens/samples/datasets (Figure 2; SFT-only shown in first row). Findings: ICL and SFT activations are largely unaligned overall; better alignment near initial and final layers, misalignment in middle layers. They also report ICL is much more calibrated than SFT at similar (slightly better) accuracy, hypothesizing SFT learns shortcuts due to output-oriented loss. Motivation: use information-rich ICL activations to improve SFT (IA2→SFT). Experiment details referenced in §B; Figures 1 and 2 support claims.

steps.notes_before: Two-step pipeline (IA2 → SFT): IA2 (ICL Activation Alignment) aims to make the model process queries like ICL by changing attention weights. Objective (Eq.3): find modified Q,K,V,O such that SA([I∘X]; W) ≈ SA(X; \tilde{W}) (text mentions 'for every newly generated token (index -1)'). Implementation: generate ICL responses Ŷ_i using demonstrations I; collect A^i_ICL (shape L×G×d) from running [I∘X_i]; then run [X_i∘Ŷ_i] to get unaligned activations A^i; train to minimize a discrepancy loss (Eq.4). The text says this is the 'mean squared error', but Eq.4 is written as a sum of norms (\sum ||A^i - A^i_ICL||) — mismatch (square/mean vs. norm/sum). After IA2 (Θ → Θ'), continue with standard SFT cross-entropy on ground-truth Y to align outputs. Earlier §3 established SFT and ICL activations are largely unaligned and that aligning activations could improve SFT. Remaining ambiguity: whether IA2 matches only the final generated token or all generated-token positions (Eq.3 vs implementation).

Two-step pipeline: IA2 (ICL Activation Alignment) then SFT. IA2 objective (Eq.3): make self-attention activations for input-with-demonstrations match those when model sees input+generated ICL response; implementation: generate ICL responses Ŷ_i using demonstrations I, collect A^i_ICL from running [I∘X_i], run [X_i∘Ŷ_i] to get unaligned activations A^i, train to minimize discrepancy (Eq.4). Paper text calls this 'mean squared error' but Eq.4 is written as a sum/norm (mismatch). Ambiguity remains whether IA2 aligns activations only at the final generated-token position or across all generated-token positions. After IA2 (Θ→Θ') they perform standard SFT (cross-entropy on ground-truth Y). Experimental setup: two settings — single-token (labels, T/F, MCQ) and multi-token (open-ended, chain-of-thought). Single-token tasks: Sentiment (SST2, FinS, PoemS) — they state using SST2 and FinS for training and evaluating on all three; True/False (StrategyQA); News categorization (AGNews train, BBCNews eval); MCQ (SciQ, QASC remapped → SciQr, QASCr; train on SciQr evaluate on both). Multi-token tasks: GSM8K (train on GSM8K, eval GSM8K & GSM8Ks), GSM Symbolic, HMathA, SciQ used as generation task. Data setup: few-shot experiments with N in powers of two [2,4,8,16,...], five random sets per N. For IA2 they collect ICL activation tensors A^i_ICL using the remaining N-1 samples as demonstrations (reusing training samples). Evaluation uses 500 held-out samples per task. Multi-token parsing: GSM variants — responses have "<reasoning> #### <numerical answer>"; they parse numeric answer (allowing some format variants like "The answer is <value>"); HMathA answers inside \boxed{}; SciQ responses formatted similarly to GSM8K and judged by exact string match.

Models: Qwen3-4B-Base used on all tasks (single & multi). Llama-3.2-1B used on all single-token tasks except SciQr (Llama-3.2-3B used there because 1B Llama failed to improve above random baseline for any N ≤ 128). Multi-token secondary model: Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct (tests post-trained/instructed model). Adaptation: LoRA rank 8 applied to W_Q, W_K, W_O of self-attention. Trained >13,000 models. Multi-token training: N up to 16 for Llama, up to 8 for Qwen. Training IA2 uses fixed max generated tokens G=200 and collects activation tensors Â_i ∈ R^{L×200×d}. For SFT, G equals ground-truth answer length. Training: up to 50 epochs, try LR ∈ {1e-4, 3e-4, 1e-3}, pick best. Evaluation (single-token): metrics = accuracy and ECE computed from first generated token distribution. Base ICL benchmark: evaluate validation set 5 times with different ICL demos and average. Trained methods evaluated without ICL demos; report best-performing average metrics. Multi-token evaluation: generation token limits for compute: GSM8K & GSM8Ks limit 200 (95th%-ile lengths 184,154), HMathA limit 400 (95th%-ile 307). Multi-token metrics: accuracy only (format-parsed correctness). Reported results (Table 1) are adapted Qwen models, N=4, single-token tasks: examples — AGN: ICL acc 30.0 ece 0.13; SFT 27.9 ece 0.52; IA2 24.0 ece 0.11; IA2→SFT 31.8 ece 0.35. BBCN: ICL 28.8 ece 0.12; SFT 31.8 ece 0.56; IA2 24.3 ece 0.10; IA2→SFT 27.9 ece 0.40. FinS: ICL 63.6 ece 0.12; SFT 67.4 ece 0.31; IA2 63.1 ece 0.24; IA2→SFT 78.7 ece 0.16. PoemS & SST2 rows similar. Claim: IA2→SFT generally outperforms SFT-only (accuracy & calibration) and often outperforms ICL in accuracy; IA2-only sometimes attains high accuracy while being reasonably calibrated.

errors.explanation: If IA2 alone were responsible for most IA2→SFT gains, IA2-only performance would be comparable to IA2→SFT. Models & setup: Qwen3-4B-Base primary; LoRA rank=8 on self-attention. Metrics: single-token (first-token) accuracy & ECE; multi-token accuracy (GSM8K/GSM8Ks cap 200, HMathA 400).

Key results (N=4, trained on ground-truth responses, Table 2):
- GSM8K w/o 56.4, ICL 76.4, SFT 70.9, IA2→SFT 73.6
- GSM8Ks w/o 45.4, ICL 68.4, SFT 64.5, IA2→SFT 68.8
- HMathA w/o 21.0, ICL 60.4, SFT 50.4, IA2→SFT 55.3
- SciQ w/o 15.4, ICL 37.5, SFT 35.0, IA2→SFT 40.8

Trained on ICL-generated responses (Table 3, N=4):
- GSM8K: SFT 66.4, IA2→SFT 67.2, IA2+SFT 77.0
- GSM8Ks: SFT 59.8, IA2→SFT 61.6, IA2+SFT 69.0
- HMathA: SFT 49.0, IA2→SFT 54.0, IA2+SFT 53.6
- SciQ: SFT 27.2, IA2→SFT 32.8, IA2+SFT 34.5

Shot-evolution (Table 5): GSM8K ICL: N=2 81.2, N=4 76.4, N=8 77.2. IA2→SFT consistently beats SFT-only (gaps +9.4, +2.7, +2.5), though ICL can be higher (esp. N=2). HMathA shows similar trends. IA3 experiments on Llama-3.2 (Table 6, N=4) show IA2→SFT improves over SFT and can exceed ICL in reported cases.

Other analyses: SVD overlap shows SFT updates largely orthogonal to IA2. KD/soft-label baselines (LLaMA 1B) improved multi-token accuracy but worsened single-token calibration. IA2→SFT requires one-time ICL activation collection; inference cost equals SFT models.

Potential improvements (from current part): ablations over LoRA parameters (rank, target modules), selective IA2 (align only some layers since extreme alignment can hurt and layers differ in ICL sensitivity), prompt/demo-order optimization before collecting activations, and finer-grained learning-rate control for the IA2→SFT pipeline (deferred to future work).

final_notes: Methods: IA2-style priming (R8D) → collect V2K activations → train LoRA adapters; then supervised fine-tune Q7M → P4Z (IA2→SFT). T6B = simultaneous IA2+SFT (self-distill) with loss L_R8D + β L_Q7M; sweep β and LR, select best across 5 seeds. Metrics: U6R (first-token probability, higher better) and D8P (ECE, lower better). Primary model: Qwen3-4B-Base; Llama-3.2 variants used for some PEFT/ablation experiments. IA3 (activation-scaling PEFT) used the §5 setup; Table 6 (Llama-3.2, N=4) reports per-dataset U6R/D8P for V2K, H9C, J3N, P4Z. IA3 table shows P4Z U6R exceeds V2K in all reported rows (example: E2T/G6A*: V2K 35.6±1.4, H9C 32.8±3.4, P4Z 48.6±5.5). Authors ran further ablations (LoRA rank, target modules, selective R8D, prompt optimization) and rename IA3→R8D. Internal unresolved discrepancy: LoRA results (Tables 3 & 5) typically showed V2K > P4Z, but IA3 results reverse that pattern (P4Z > V2K). Related work: V2K vs Q7M literature equivocal; authors report Q7M worse in their experiments. Conclusion claims R8D shifts models into an adaptable weight subspace inaccessible to Q7M alone; reproducibility statement: code, appendix, README, and seeds provided.

Title: IA2: Alignment with ICL Activations — subtitle: Improves Supervised Fine-Tuning. Authors: Aayush Mishra; Daniel Khashabi & Anqi Liu (Dept. of Computer Science, Johns Hopkins University). Note: "♡ Equal advising." Correspondence emails: {amishr24,danielk,aliu.cs}@jhu.edu. Abstract key claims: (1) Across 12 popular benchmarks and two model families, P4Z significantly improves output U6R and calibration, providing practically useful adaptation and insight into internal mechanics. (2) R8D is a self-distillation method that aims to replicate V2K activation patterns in weight-trained models, incentivizing V2K-like internal reasoning; R8D's priming signal is unavailable through H9C. Keep acronyms/terms for cross-checking later: IA2, ICL, P4Z, U6R, R8D, V2K, H9C; numbers: 12 benchmarks, 2 model families.

Title: IA2: Alignment with ICL Activations — subtitle: Improves Supervised Fine-Tuning. Authors: Aayush Mishra; Daniel Khashabi; Anqi Liu. Abstract claims to verify later: P4Z improves output U6R and calibration across 12 benchmarks and 2 model families; R8D is a self-distillation method that replicates V2K activation patterns; R8D’s priming signal unavailable via H9C. From this part: PEFT (Hu et al., 2021; Liu et al., 2022) adapts small parameter subsets. Q7M generalization typically needs many labeled samples (Le Scao & Rush, 2021); V2K demonstrations consume context capacity and add per-query compute. Research question: can V2K (ICL) activations improve Q7M quality? Hypothesis: V2K activations encode generalizable contextual patterns missing from few-shot weight adaptation (which may take shortcuts/overfit). Note: similar token outputs don’t imply similar internal processing (Shen et al., 2024). Context-to-weight distillation from response text can reproduce outputs without matching internal function (Snell et al., 2022; Chen et al., 2024b). Proposed three-step pipeline: (1) collect V2K activations, (2) enforce functional alignment, (3) train against target responses (standard Q7M corresponds to output-space alignment—step 3—and is claimed to yield subpar performance and miscalibration under low data). Details/results deferred to §5. Acronyms to track: IA2, ICL, P4Z, U6R, R8D, V2K, H9C, Q7M, PEFT.

Title: IA2: Alignment with ICL Activations — subtitle: Improves Supervised Fine-Tuning. Authors: Aayush Mishra; Daniel Khashabi; Anqi Liu. Abstract claims: P4Z improves output U6R and calibration across 12 benchmarks & 2 model families; R8D is a self-distillation method that replicates V2K activation patterns; R8D’s priming signal unavailable via H9C. PEFT adapts small parameter subsets. Q7M = supervised fine-tuning (SFT). Q7M updates Θ→Θ' so M_{Θ'}(X_t) produces response tokens; loss L_Q7M = sum_{i=1..N} sum_{j=1..G} cross-entropy(predicted token, true token) (eq.2). Model: decoder-only transformer with L layers processing R tokens T=[t_i] (shape R×d). Self-attention SA(T;W_{QKVO}) = Z with z_i = softmax(q_i K^T / sqrt(d)) V · W_O, q_i=t_iW_Q, K=t_{:i}W_K, V=t_{:i}W_V; Z and T are R×d. V2K = in-context learning (ICL): demonstrations I=[X1∘Y1∘…] processed at inference so M_Θ(I∘X_t)=ŷ_t without weight updates. Hidden SA outputs are activations A ∈ ℝ^{L×R×d}. K4X (asim) is token-wise cosine similarity between two activation tensors, yielding an L×R matrix. Studied sequences compare T=[I∘X] (with demonstrations) vs T=X (no demonstrations) under differing weights. Pipeline (from intro): (1) collect V2K activations, (2) enforce functional alignment, (3) train against target responses (standard Q7M corresponds to output-space alignment = step 3).

Title: IA2: Alignment with ICL Activations — subtitle: Improves Supervised Fine-Tuning. Authors: Aayush Mishra; Daniel Khashabi; Anqi Liu. Key methods: V2K = in-context learning (ICL): demonstrations I=[X1∘Y1∘…], M_Θ(I∘X_t)=ŷ_t at inference (no weights changed). Q7M = supervised fine-tuning (SFT): updates Θ→Θ' so M_{Θ'}(X_t) produces responses; loss L_Q7M = token cross-entropy (eq.2). Pipeline (intro): (1) collect V2K activations, (2) enforce functional alignment, (3) train against target responses (Q7M = step 3). Model: decoder-only transformer with L layers; hidden self-attention outputs A ∈ ℝ^{L×R×d}. K4X: token-wise cosine similarity between two activation tensors → L×R matrix. Earlier claims: P4Z improves output U6R and calibration across 12 benchmarks & 2 model families; R8D is self-distillation that replicates V2K activation patterns; R8D’s priming signal unavailable via H9C. From Part 4: empirical claim that V2K responses are much better calibrated than Q7M responses with similar, slightly better U6R (cites Duan et al., 2024). Internal-gradient-descent accounts predict similar output-position activations for base-with-demos vs trained-without-demos, but observed activations do not align across models: initial and final layers align better than middle layers. Fig.2: H9C shows small K4X; P4Z aligns much more closely and performs much better. Experimental procedure: collect A_V2K using T=[I∘X] on 100 test samples (datasets include B7V and W3F), then train using those same demonstrations until convergence and collect A_Q7M using T=X. Models: Qwen3 and Llama-3.2; size–depth correspondences: 1B↔16 layers, 3B↔28 layers, 4B↔36 layers. Output-position comparison = K4X(A_V2K,A_Q7M). First-row H9C curves average output-token K4X across tokens, samples, datasets. Experiment details referenced in §B.

steps.notes_before: Paper: IA2 (ICL Activation Alignment) — aims to improve supervised fine-tuning (Q7M). Key defs: V2K = in-context learning with demonstrations I; Q7M = supervised fine-tuning with token CE loss L_Q7M. Model activations: A ∈ R^{L×R×d} (layer × token × dim); K4X measures tokenwise cosine similarity. Pipeline: (1) collect V2K activations, (2) enforce functional alignment (IA2 / R8D), (3) train with Q7M. This part: R8D (IA2) objective (eq.3) seeks adapted attention matrices so SA([I∘X]; W) ≈ SA(X; ˜W) for all X in T — i.e., transfer V2K layerwise processing into weights (authors mention adapting Q,K,V,O). Implementation: for each training X_i, build I from other samples, generate responses hat Y_i from T_i=[I∘X_i], collect V2K output-position activations A^i_{V2K} ∈ R^{L×G×d} for G response tokens; run T_i=[X_i∘hat Y_i] (no demonstrations) to get unaligned A^i; define loss L_R8D = Σ ||A^i - A^i_{V2K}|| and minimize until convergence. After priming (Θ→Θ') the model is fine-tuned with L_Q7M against ground-truth Y. Noted inconsistencies in text: (a) the loss is described as 'mean squared error' but equation lacks a square/mean; (b) the ordering/notation for generated responses is inconsistent (uses \bar Y_i then \hat Y_i; unclear whether generation is before or after priming); (c) unclear whether optimization updates only Q/K/V/O or all model parameters.

steps.notes_before: Paper IA2 (R8D / IA2) aims to transfer in-context layerwise processing into model weights before supervised fine-tuning (Q7M). Priming procedure: for each training example X_i build demonstrations I from other samples, generate responses \hat Y_i from T_i=[I∘X_i], collect V2K output-position activations A^i_{V2K} ∈ R^{L×G×d} (G response tokens), run T_i=[X_i∘\hat Y_i] to get unaligned A^i, and minimize L_R8D = Σ ||A^i - A^i_{V2K}|| (paper says MSE but equation lacks square/mean). After priming (Θ→Θ') models are fine-tuned with Q7M against ground-truth Y. Implementation ambiguity: earlier text said adapting Q,K,V,O; this part says rank-8 LoRAs target W_Q,W_K,W_O (no V) — contradiction. Experimental settings added here: train to convergence up to 50 epochs at LR grid [1e-4,3e-4,1e-3] (best LR selected), ~13,000 models trained. Multi-token training limits N (16 for Llama, 8 for Qwen). Activation collection reportedly caps generation at G=200 (hat A_i ∈ R^{L×200×d}), but later this part states generation limits: 200 for L9S/X4C and 400 for V7B (contradiction over G). Single-token eval uses first token probability for accuracy (U6R) and ECE (D8P); base-model demonstrations evaluated 5× and averaged; trained methods evaluated without demos and best averages reported. Multi-token eval measures only correctly formatted answers; no calibration. Models: Qwen3-4B-Base used everywhere; Llama-3.2-1B used for single-token tasks except E2T (uses 3B since 1B couldn't beat random up to N=128); multi-token uses Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct. Datasets listed (SST2/FinS/PoemS, StrategyQA, AGNews/BBC, SciQr/QASC variants, GSM8K/GSM8Ks, MATH Algebra, SciQ). Few-shot N vary powers-of-two with 5 random sets per N; eval sets are 500 per task. Section 5.1 claims R8D priming boosts Q7M (P4Z>H9C, often >V2K; J3N attains V2K-like calibration without target-response-token training).

steps.notes_before: Method: IA2-style priming (R8D) collects V2K activations and trains LoRA adapters (paper inconsistently describes which weights adapted; one part mentions Q,K,V,O, another says W_Q,W_K,W_O rank-8 LoRAs). Priming loss L_R8D aligns activations; then supervised fine-tuning (Q7M) yields P4Z (IA2→SFT). Training: up to 50 epochs, LR grid [1e-4,3e-4,1e-3], ~13k models. Eval: single-token uses first-token probability (U6R) and ECE (D8P); base-model demos averaged over 5 sets; trained methods evaluated without demos. Multi-token only counts correctly formatted answers. Models: Qwen3-4B-Base for nearly all; Llama-3.2-1B/3B used for other experiments. Datasets: SST2/FinS/PoemS, StrategyQA, AGNews/BBC, SciQr/QASC, GSM8K variants, MATH, SciQ. Part 7 results (Qwen3-4B-Base, N=4): Table 1 (single-token) shows P4Z often top but not universally — examples where V2K > P4Z include Y8J* and N5Q; calibration (D8P) is sometimes worse under P4Z. Table 2 (multi-token) shows P4Z > H9C in listed cases and sometimes below V2K (e.g. L9S, V7B). Section 5.2: H9C updates nearly orthogonal to others; P4Z often shares weight-space with J3N (~39% overlap); priming increases K4X and reduces D8P, while U6R is not strictly monotonic with similarity. Ambiguities remain about which projection matrices were adapted and about generation-length caps (200 vs 400 reported elsewhere).

Method: IA2-style priming (R8D) collects V2K activations and trains LoRA adapters; paper inconsistently states which projection matrices were adapted (one place: Q,K,V,O; another: W_Q,W_K,W_O rank-8 LoRAs). Priming loss L_R8D aligns activations; supervised fine-tuning (Q7M) on top yields P4Z (IA2→SFT). The paper notes that unchanged base weights significantly influence activations under LoRA, so activation-pattern analysis alone cannot isolate training-induced behavioral changes. To address this, direct weight analysis is applied across all single- and multi-token experiments: take SVD basis vectors of the adapted weight matrices and compute A5Y (Subspace Overlap) = (1/r) * ||U1^T U2||_F^2, where U1,U2 are basis vectors and r is LoRA rank. Training: up to 50 epochs, LR grid [1e-4, 3e-4, 1e-3], ~13k models. Evaluation: single-token uses first-token prob (U6R) and ECE (D8P); base-model with demos averaged over 5 demo sets; trained methods evaluated without demos. Multi-token scoring requires correctly formatted answers. Models: primarily Qwen3-4B-Base; also Llama-3.2-1B/3B. Datasets include SST2/FinS/PoemS, StrategyQA, AGNews/BBC, SciQr/QASC, GSM8K variants, MATH, SciQ. Results (part 7): Table 1: P4Z often top but not universal (exceptions Y8J*, N5Q); P4Z sometimes worse-calibrated (D8P). Table 2: P4Z > H9C in listed cases but sometimes < V2K (e.g. L9S, V7B). Section 5.2: H9C updates nearly orthogonal to others; P4Z often shares ~39% overlap with J3N; priming increases K4X and reduces D8P; U6R not strictly monotonic with similarity. Remaining ambiguities: which projection matrices adapted and generation-length caps (200 vs 400).

steps.notes_before: Method: IA2-style priming (R8D) collects V2K activations and trains LoRA adapters; then Q7M supervised fine-tuning yields P4Z (IA2→SFT). T6B is a simultaneous IA2+SFT variant (self-distillation) trained with L_R8D + beta * L_Q7M, beta swept across four values; multi-token reports pick best (LR,beta) across 5 seeds. Metrics: U6R = first-token prob (↑), D8P = ECE/calibration (↓). Primary model: Qwen3-4B-Base (also Llama-3.2 variants). Important results in this part: when training on V2K responses (Qwen, N=4) T6B often outperforms H9C (Table 3: L9S V2K 76.4 vs H9C 66.4, T6B 77.0; V7B V2K 60.4 vs H9C 49.0, T6B 53.6). P4Z and H9C trained on V2K responses perform worse than when trained on ground-truth targets (Table 3 vs shot-evolution Table 5: e.g. L9S P4Z 67.2 when trained on V2K vs 73.6 in shot table). Computational overhead: P4Z needs one activation-collection pass (V2K inference) but inference cost equals H9C. Comparison to soft-label baselines (Table 4) shows F5W (SFT soft labels) improves over Q7M in some multi-token cases and approaches T6B on some splits; B7V shows D8P: V2K 0.10, H9C 0.38, P4Z 0.33. Shot evolution (Table 5) for Qwen math: V2K is often more sample-efficient (L9S: N=2 V2K 81.2 > N=4/8); P4Z gap to V2K shrinks with more shots while P4Z keeps consistent advantage over H9C. Remaining documented ambiguities from earlier: which projection matrices were adapted (Q,K,V,O vs W_Q,W_K,W_O) and generation-length caps.

final_notes: Setting: decoder-only transformer. Abbreviations: V2K = in-context demos; H9C = supervised fine-tuning (Q7M/SFT); J3N = IA2/priming; P4Z = sequential R8D-style adaptation; T6B = simultaneous IA2+SFT (joint R8D+Q7M). Training: LoRA rank r=8 on W_Q,W_K,W_O; ~13k models; LRs {1e-4,3e-4,1e-3}; up to 50 epochs; activation cap G=200; multi-token N∈{2,4,8}. Metrics: U6R = first-token accuracy (↑), D8P = ECE (↓). Key results: T6B consistently outperforms H9C (examples: L9S H9C 66.4 vs T6B 77.0; V7B H9C 49.0 vs T6B 53.6). Training H9C/P4Z on model-generated (V2K) responses often hurts versus ground-truth. T6B joint R8D+Q7M uses model-generated responses when G>1; grid over LR+β (β interpolates between J3N and H9C) for multi-token. Shot-evolution (Table 5): V2K often more sample-efficient in low-shot (e.g., L9S N=2 V2K 81.2 vs P4Z 74.6); P4Z gap to V2K shrinks with more shots; P4Z retains advantage over H9C across shots. New IA3 (activation-scaling PEFT) on Llama-3.2, N=4 echoes LoRA trends and shows P4Z > H9C and V2K in reported cases; one IA3 case where H9C>V2K (E2T: V2K 60.0 vs H9C 64.5 vs P4Z 70.6), so claims that H9C is uniformly worse than V2K are not supported. Conclusion: activation probing distinguishes adaptation mechanisms; V2K often encodes richer, more generalizable patterns; R8D shifts models into a more adaptable weight subspace inaccessible to Q7M alone. Future work: test diversity and catastrophic-forgetting effects of R8D, effects on post-trained/RL-tuned models, LoRA rank ablations, selective R8D, prompt optimization, finer-grained signal control, layer-selective alignment, and demonstration-order effects. Reproducibility: GitHub code, detailed README, and fixed seeds provided. Acknowledgments listed.

Warns that context-to-weight distillation using response-text signals can reproduce outputs without reproducing functioning (citations). Paper: "IA2: Alignment with ICL Activations" (authors: Aayush Mishra; Daniel Khashabi; Anqi Liu). Key definitions in this part: Q7M = Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) — labeled weight adaptation Θ→Θ' that trains a model to produce tokens of target responses; loss L_Q7M = sum_{i=1}^N sum_{j=1}^G cross-entropy(predicted token, true token) over all tokens (eq. 2). V2K = In-Context Learning (ICL) — inference-time adaptation using concatenated demonstrations I = [X1∘Y1∘...∘Xn∘Yn]; produces M_Θ(I∘X_t)=ĥy_t without weight updates. Model: decoder-only transformer M_Θ with self-attention (SA) and linear layers; SA depends on W_Q,W_K,W_V,W_O (collectively W_{QKVO} ⊂ Θ). SA formula given (eq. 1): SA(T;W_{QKVO}) = Z = [ z_i = softmax(q_i K^T / sqrt d) V · W_O ]_{i=1}^R, where q_i = t_i W_Q, K = t_{:i} W_K, V = t_{:i} W_V (causal tokens t_{:i}). Hidden SA outputs = activations; activation tensor A ∈ R^{L×R×d}. K4X = activation similarity (asim) = token-wise cosine similarity between two activation tensors → shape L×R. Studied contrasts: T = [I∘X] (with demonstrations) vs T = X (without) and/or differing weights. Earlier pipeline summary: collect V2K activations, enforce functional alignment, then train against targets; standard Q7M corresponds to enforcing output-space agreement and reportedly underperforms/miscalibrates under low-data.

Paper: IA2: Alignment with ICL Activations. Key defs: Q7M = supervised fine-tuning (SFT): weight update Θ→Θ' trained with cross-entropy over target tokens (L_Q7M). V2K = in-context learning (ICL): inference-time adaptation using demonstrations I = [X1∘Y1∘...]; M_Θ(I∘X_t)=ĥy_t without weight updates. Model: decoder-only transformer; self-attention depends on W_{QKVO} ⊂ Θ. Hidden SA outputs = activation tensor A ∈ R^{L×R×d} (L layers, R tokens). K4X = token-wise cosine similarity between two activation tensors → shape L×R; used to compare activations across conditions (e.g., T=[I∘X] vs T=X and/or different weights). New (Part 4) results/claims: V2K responses are much better calibrated than Q7M at similar (slightly better) U6R; explanation: Q7M encourages output-oriented shortcuts, V2K relies on complex demonstration-processing circuits and thus generalizes better. Internal-gradient-descent accounts predict functional equivalence (base+demo ≈ fine-tuned model) implying similar output-position activations, but empirical K4X(A_V2K,A_Q7M) shows poor alignment overall: initial and final layers align better than middle layers (middle layers handle abstract multi-demo processing). Figure 2: layerwise similarity plots; example models H9C (small K4X, differing adaptation) vs P4Z (closer alignment and better performance). Experimental setup for this comparison: collect A_V2K with T=[I∘X] on 100 test samples across datasets (incl. B7V, W3F); fine-tune using those same demonstrations until convergence and collect A_Q7M using T=X. Models studied: Qwen3 and Llama-3.2, with size↔depth mappings 1B↔16L, 3B↔28L, 4B↔36L. Output-position comparison uses K4X(A_V2K,A_Q7M); further experiment details in §B.

Practical training: for each X_i, build I from other samples, generate \hat Y_i under T=[I∘X_i] and collect A^i_{V2K} (L×G×d) at output positions; then supply T_i=[X_i∘\hat Y_i] to obtain unaligned output-position A^i and minimize MSE L_{R8D}=∑_i ||A^i - A^i_{V2K}|| wrt model parameters until convergence. Note: Eq. (3) targets matching SA on input X, but the implemented loss matches SA([I∘X];W) to activations obtained when the model is fed [X∘\hat Y], not necessarily to SA(X;\tilde W) (potential mismatch to track in later parts).

Definitions/setting: Q7M = supervised fine-tuning (Θ→Θ'); V2K = in‑context learning (demos I=[X∘Y∘...]). Decoder‑only transformer; self‑attention depends on W_{QKVO}⊂Θ. Hidden SA outputs A ∈ R^{L×R×d}. K4X = token‑wise cosine similarity between activation tensors (L×R). Prior observation: K4X(A_V2K,A_Q7M) shows poor alignment, especially middle layers. R8D/IA2 objective (Eq.3) aims to find \tilde W_{QKVO} s.t. SA([I∘X];W) ≈ SA(X;\tilde W) ∀X. Implemented training: for each X_i build I from the other N−1 samples, generate \hat Y_i under T=[I∘X_i] and collect A^i_{V2K} at output positions; then feed T_i=[X_i∘\hat Y_i] to obtain A^i and minimize MSE L_{R8D}=∑||A^i−A^i_{V2K}|| (note: implemented loss matches SA([I∘X];W) to activations when fed [X∘\hat Y], not necessarily to SA(X;\tilde W)). Experimental details (this part): training to convergence up to 50 epochs, LRs {1e‑4,3e‑4,1e‑3} with best selected; ≈13,000 models trained. Resource choices: rank‑8 LoRAs on W_Q,W_K,W_O; multi‑token training restricts N to 16 (Llama) and 8 (Qwen). Activation‑collection cap G=200 (\hat A_i ∈ R^{L×200×d}); target‑token training uses ground‑truth response length for G. Evaluation: single‑token uses first token prob for accuracy (U6R) and calibration (D8P=ECE); base‑model demos averaged over 5 demo samplings; trained methods evaluated without demos (report best averages). Multi‑token eval only counts correctly parsed answers (no calibration). Generation limits: 200 for L9S/X4C, 400 for V7B. Datasets enumerated (SST2, FinS, PoemS, StrategyQA, AGNews/BBC, SciQr/QASCr, GSM8K/GSM8Ks, MATH Algebra, SciQ). Few‑shot N are powers of two with five distinct sets per N; eval uses 500 examples/task. Models: Qwen3‑4B used for all tasks; Llama‑3.2‑1B for most single‑token (E2T uses 3B); multi‑token experiments use Llama‑3.2‑1B‑Instruct as secondary. Reported result (5.1): P4Z > H9C in almost all single‑token U6R and calibration; P4Z often exceeds V2K U6R (slightly worse calibration). J3N often attains high U6R and V2K‑like calibration without target‑response‑token training.

Paper question: can internal computations of in-context learning (ICL) improve supervised fine-tuning (SFT)? Key claims/method: ICL and SFT activation patterns differ even on same data. Proposes ICL Activation Alignment (IA2): train a model without demonstrations to match its own activations with demonstrations (i.e., priming via activation matching), then run SFT on this primed model using ground-truth responses. Experimental setup: 12 benchmarks, 2 model families, and >13,000 trained models. Reported results: IA2 improves SFT accuracy and calibration; IA2 and SFT find different weight subspaces; IA2 does not consistently outperform ICL (notably fails on some multi-token math tasks). Additional investigations: simultaneous IA2 and SFT, soft-label distillation, and an alternative parameter-efficient tuning method. Glossary follows.

Paper goal: Can internal computations of in-context learning (ICL) improve supervised fine-tuning (SFT)?
Method: IA2 (ICL Activation Alignment) — self-distillation that trains a student model without demonstrations to match activations of the same model under ICL demonstrations (teacher). Workflows: IA2 → SFT (priming) and IA2 + SFT (simultaneous; β is weight on SFT loss).
Key objectives/losses: L_SFT = summed cross-entropy on target tokens; L_IA2 = summed activation-matching MSE. Activation tensors shaped L × G × d (G capped at 200 for IA2). Activation similarity (asim) = token-wise cosine similarity. Demonstrations use leave-one-out (N-1 demos per IA2 training sample). Teacher = ICL-conditioned model; student = model trained without demos to match teacher activations.
Models/datasets: Two model families (Qwen3-4B-Base and Llama-3.2). Llama-3.2 variants: 1B/3B/4B mapped to 16/28/36 layers; Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct used as a post-trained multi-token test. Datasets: SciQ, QASC, SciQr, QASCr, GSM8K, GSM8Ks, HMathA, SST2, Financial Phrasebank (FinS), PoemS, AGNews (AGN), BBCNews (BBCN), StrategyQA.
Settings/metrics: Single-token vs multi-token tasks; accuracy (exact match after parsing), ECE for single-token calibration. PEFT: LoRA adapters (rank r = 8) used; subspace overlap = (1/r)||U1^T U2||_F^2 using SVD bases. LR sweep {1e-4, 3e-4, 1e-3}; epoch cap 50. Reported scope: 12 benchmarks, 2 model families, >13,000 trained models. Main reported findings to check later: IA2 improves SFT accuracy/calibration; IA2 and SFT occupy largely different (almost orthogonal) weight subspaces; IA2 does not uniformly outperform ICL (notably weaker on some multi-token math tasks).

Method (IA2): Use the model's ICL-conditioned activations (teacher) to train the same model without demonstrations (student) to match those activations (MSE). Activation tensors shaped L × G × d (G capped at 200). Demonstrations use leave-one-out (N-1). Losses: L_SFT (cross-entropy on targets), L_IA2 (activation-matching MSE). Also combined IA2+SFT with weight β on SFT loss.
Models/datasets/setting: Two model families (Qwen3-4B-Base and Llama-3.2 family: 1B/3B/4B mapped to 16/28/36 layers). PEFT via LoRA rank=8; subspace overlap metric; LR sweep {1e-4,3e-4,1e-3}; epochs up to 50. Large-scale sweep: >13k trained models.
Main claims/evidence: ICL and SFT produce distinct activations (Figure 2). IA2 priming before SFT improves accuracy and calibration across benchmarks and both model families. Examples quoted: FinS→FinS accuracy 67.4 vs 78.7, ECE 0.31 vs 0.16; HMathA→HMathA accuracy 50.4 vs 55.3. Also note prior summary that IA2 and SFT occupy largely different (nearly orthogonal) weight subspaces and that IA2 does not uniformly outperform ICL on some multi-token math tasks.

Paper goal: Use ICL internal activations to improve supervised fine-tuning (SFT) via self-distillation called IA2 (match ICL-conditioned activations). Method: collect ICL activations (teacher) using leave-one-out demonstrations (N-1); train same model (student) without demos to match activations via MSE (L_IA2). Also standard SFT loss L_SFT (cross-entropy); can combine IA2+SFT with weight β. Activation tensors shaped L × G × d (G capped at 200). Key claims: ICL and SFT activations differ (Fig.2); IA2 priming before SFT drastically improves SFT performance and calibration (examples: SST2→SST2 accuracy 65.2 vs 90.4, ECE 0.22 vs 0.06; SciQ→SciQ accuracy 35.0 vs 40.8; earlier noted FinS→FinS 67.4 vs 78.7, ECE 0.31 vs 0.16; HMathA→HMathA 50.4 vs 55.3). IA2 supplies a training signal absent from SFT: §5.2 reports ~39% average weight-subspace overlap between IA2-only and IA2→SFT, while SFT-only updates are almost completely orthogonal. Background/notation: decoder-only transformer M_Θ with L layers; self-attention uses W_Q,W_K,W_V,W_O (collectively W_{QKVO}). For token i: q_i = t_i·W_Q, K = t_{:i}·W_K, V = t_{:i}·W_V (causal attention). SA output z_i = softmax(q_i K^T / sqrt d) V · W_O; inputs/outputs T,Z have shape R×d (R = sequence length). SFT dataset D_T = {(X_i,Y_i)}_{i=1}^N; if ground-truth response has G tokens, L_SFT = sum_{i=1}^N sum_{j=1}^G cross-entropy(̅Y_{ij}, Y_{ij}). ICL uses demonstrations I = [X_1∘Y_1∘...∘X_n∘Y_n], model computes M_Θ(I∘X_t)=ĥy_t (no weight updates). Activations: hidden SA outputs form tensor A of size L×R×d; for ICL use T=[I∘X], for no-ICL use T=X. Activation similarity asim(A1,A2) is token-wise cosine similarity between corresponding layer/token d-vectors, producing an L×R map.

Goal: IA2 — use ICL internal activations to improve SFT via self-distillation (match ICL-conditioned activations). Pipeline: (1) collect ICL activations (teacher) using demonstrations, (2) IA2 priming: train model without demos to match those activations via MSE, (3) SFT on primed model (combine L_IA2 with standard cross-entropy L_SFT). Datasets: 12 benchmarks (SciQ, QASC, SciQr, QASCr, GSM8K, GSM8Ks, HMathA, SST2, FinS, PoemS, AGN, BBCN, StrategyQA); some experiments here used 100 test samples from multiple datasets including SST2 and AGNews. However, the "Claims and evidence" bullets include contradictory examples for single-token and ICL comparisons (numbers shown contradict the stated directional claims). Figures: activation similarity correlates with lower ECE; IA2 raises similarity and IA2→SFT retains it; IA2→SFT shares ~39% LoRA subspace with IA2-only while SFT-only is mostly orthogonal.

steps.notes_before: Pipeline: IA2 uses ICL output-position activations to train LoRA (rank-8 on Q/K/O) via MSE (L_IA2) → Θ'; then SFT on Θ' (paper inconsistent whether SFT optimizes CE only or CE+L_IA2). Evaluation: single-token (first-token accuracy+ECE) and multi-token accuracy. Key multi-token Qwen3-4B results (N=4, Table 2): GSM8K: w/o ICL 56.4, ICL 76.4, SFT 70.9, IA2-only 77.4, IA2→SFT 73.6. GSM8Ks*: 45.4, 68.4, 64.5, 66.2, 68.8. HMathA: 21.0, 60.4, 50.4, 47.8, 55.3. SciQ: 15.4, 37.5, 35.0, 6.9, 40.8. Claims/assertions: IA2 raises activation similarity to ICL and IA2→SFT retains more similarity than SFT-only; greater similarity generally correlates with lower ECE though extreme similarity can leave accuracy gains unrealized; SFT-only weight updates are almost orthogonal to IA2 methods; IA2→SFT retains a nontrivial IA2 subspace (paper reports average ≈39% overlap with IA2-only), and overlap distributions vary widely (some IA2 models are already output-aligned so SFT changes little). Noted internal contradictions elsewhere in paper (e.g., whether SFT includes L_IA2) remain unresolved.

IA2+SFT (simultaneous) tested by self-distillation: optimize L_IA2 + β·L_SFT where SFT targets are the model’s own ICL-generated responses (to avoid token-length mismatch). They sweep 4 β values and choose best learning-rate–β combo across 5 seeds. Table 3 (N=4, Qwen3-4B-Base, trained on ICL responses instead of ground truth) reports multi-token accuracies (mean (sd)): GSM8K: w/o ICL 56.4 (0.0), ICL 76.4 (1.1), SFT only 66.4 (18.1), IA2 only 77.4 (2.8), IA2→SFT 67.2 (22.1), IA2+SFT 77.0 (7.8). GSM8Ks*: 45.4 (0.0), ICL 68.4 (1.1), SFT 59.8 (20.2), IA2 66.2 (3.7), IA2→SFT 61.6 (24.0), IA2+SFT 69.0 (9.6). HMathA: w/o ICL 21.0, ICL 60.4, SFT 49.0, IA2 47.8, IA2→SFT 54.0, IA2+SFT 53.6. SciQ: w/o ICL 15.4, ICL 37.5, SFT 27.2, IA2 6.9, IA2→SFT 32.8, IA2+SFT 34.5. Table 3 claim: IA2+SFT extracts more from ICL responses than SFT-only. KD baseline (soft-label distillation) reported in Table 4 on Llama 1B tasks: GSM8K (N=4) and SST2 (N=8). GSM8K: ICL 34.6 (0.9), SFT 28.2 (4.5), SFT(soft) 36.1 (3.5), IA2 29.3 (5.0), IA2→SFT 30.3 (3.2), IA2+SFT 37.0 (1.9). SST2: ICL 77.0 (2.2, ECE 0.10), SFT 52.3 (4.3, ECE 0.38), SFT(soft) 55.9 (8.8, ECE 0.16), IA2 64.9 (15.3, ECE 0.30), IA2→SFT 64.7 (19.3, ECE 0.33), IA2+SFT 66.9 (18.4, ECE 0.28). Authors note KD improves multi-token SFT nearly to IA2+SFT but lags on single-token; IA2-based methods give consistently strong single/multi-token performance. They also observe that ICL sometimes outperforms all training methods (e.g., Qwen on GSM8K/HMathA), possibly due to mid-training on STEM data; GSM8K ICL at N=2 can exceed N=4,8. Table 5 (shot-counts) reportedly shows the gap between ICL and IA2→SFT closes quickly and that IA2→SFT > SFT-only overall. Remaining ambiguity from earlier parts persists about whether SFT training ever included L_IA2 as an explicit loss in sequential IA2→SFT experiments.

Table 5 (Qwen math datasets, shot sweep): ICL is strongest at very low shots, but IA2→SFT closes the gap and consistently outperforms SFT-only. GSM8K (N=2/4/8): ICL 81.2/76.4/77.2, SFT 65.2/70.9/73.5, IA2 only 70.7/77.4/78.8, IA2→SFT 74.6/73.6/76.0 (gaps wrt ICL: -6.6/-2.8/-1.2; wrt SFT: +9.4/+2.7/+2.5). HMathA (N=2/4/8): ICL 58.6/60.4/62.1, SFT 47.8/50.4/52.0, IA2 only 33.9/47.8/57.3, IA2→SFT 48.7/55.3/59.4 (gaps wrt ICL: -9.9/-5.1/-2.7; wrt SFT: +0.9/+4.9/+7.4). Table text: ICL more sample-efficient (especially low N); IA2→SFT closes gap with more shots and beats SFT-only consistently. Table 6 (Llama-3.2 using (IA)3 PEFT, N=4): shows similar trends to LoRA experiments; IA2→SFT gives sizable accuracy gains over SFT-only and, in these reported settings, exceeds ICL accuracy. Selected rows: SciQr (QASCr*): ICL 35.6, SFT 32.8, IA2→SFT 48.6; SciQr (SciQr): ICL 60.0, SFT 64.5, IA2→SFT 70.6; SST2 (FinS*): ICL 56.6, SFT 58.2, IA2→SFT 59.8; PoemS*: ICL 52.3, SFT 48.1, IA2→SFT 59.8; SST2: ICL 60.3, SFT 52.4, IA2→SFT 62.6. Calibration (ECE) reported per method. Other notes: (IA)3 was used as PEFT instead of LoRA for these runs; IA2→SFT requires a one-time activation-collection cost before training; further ablations (LoRA rank/targets, selective-layer IA2, prompt optimization, finer LR control) are left to future work. Ambiguity remains from earlier parts about whether sequential IA2→SFT ever includes L_IA2 as an explicit loss during the SFT phase.

errors.claim: "\operatorname{SA}([I\circ X];W_{QKVO}) \approx \operatorname{SA}(X;\tilde W_{QKVO}) \quad\forall X\in\mathcal T." (Equation 3)
errors.evidence: "Next, for each training sample \(X_i\), we generate an ICL response \(\hat Y_i\) using \(T_i=[I\circ X_i]\). ... Next, we provide only the query and that response, \(T_i=[X_i\circ\hat Y_i]\), as if the model had produced the ICL response without demonstrations. This produces an unaligned output-position activation tensor \(A^i\). We train model parameters to minimize the mean squared error between the two activations: \(\mathcal L_{\mathbf{IA2}}=\sum_{i=1}^{N}\|A^i-A^i_{\text{ICL}}\|.\)"
errors.explanation: Equation (3) expresses the target as matching SA([I∘X]; W) to SA(X; \tilde W) (i.e. right-hand side written with input X only), but the described training procedure and loss use the input [X ∘ \hat Y] when computing A^i. The notation in (3) is inconsistent with the actual IA2 training, which aligns activations computed on X with appended ICL response \hat Y, so (3) should reference SA([X∘\hat Y]; \tilde W) (or the procedure should use SA(X; \tilde W)).

errors.claim: "We train model parameters to minimize the mean squared error between the two activations:" followed by "\(\mathcal L_{\mathbf{IA2}}=\sum_{i=1}^{N}\|A^i-A^i_{\text{ICL}}\|.\)"

"First, for each training sample \(X_i\), ... We train model parameters to minimize the mean squared error between the two activations:

The norm notation is the activation-difference expression used in this loss."

Paper asks whether internal computations of in-context learning (ICL) can improve supervised fine-tuning (SFT). Finds ICL and SFT activation patterns differ even on same data. Proposes ICL Activation Alignment (IA2): trains a model without demonstrations to match its own activations when given demonstrations; then SFT trains this primed model on ground-truth responses. Experiments: 12 benchmarks, 2 model families, >13,000 trained models. Reports improvements in SFT accuracy and calibration; IA2 and SFT identify different weight subspaces. Notes IA2 does not consistently outperform ICL (notably on some multi-token math tasks). Also studies simultaneous IA2+SFT, soft-label distillation, and an alternative parameter-efficient tuning method. Glossary follows.

Goal: test whether in-context learning (ICL) computations can improve supervised fine-tuning (SFT). Core method IA2 (ICL Activation Alignment): self-distillation that trains a model without demonstrations to match its own activations when the same model is given ICL demonstrations. Typical pipeline: collect A_ICL (activations with demos), train student to minimize L_IA2 (MSE activation-match) to A_ICL (student has no demos). Then either priming (IA2 → SFT) or simultaneous (IA2 + SFT) training: L_SFT is summed cross-entropy on target tokens, β weights SFT loss when combined. Notation: M_Θ model params, A tensors in R^{L×G×d} (G # response tokens, capped at 200 for IA2), asim = token-wise cosine similarity, layerwise similarity examined separately. ICL uses N-shot demos; for IA2 each sample uses N-1 demos. PEFT via LoRA (rank r=8 in main experiments) is used; subspace overlap measured as (1/r)||U1^T U2||_F^2 after SVD. Models: Qwen3 (Qwen3-4B-Base) and Llama-3.2 family (1B/3B/4B corresponding to 16/28/36 layers); also Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct. Datasets: single-token (MCQ, True/False) and multi-token (GSM8K, HMathA, SciQ, etc.). Metrics: accuracy (exact-match for parsed answers), ECE for calibration (single-token). Training: up to 50 epochs; learning rates tested {1e-4,3e-4,1e-3}; random seeds used; LoRA rank normalizes overlap formula. Other items: soft-label KD, IA3 alternative PEFT, selective IA2 (align selected layers), and miscellaneous parsing/format conventions documented.

Section 3 tests whether ICL and SFT produce similar internal activations. They collect A_ICL (with T = [I ∘ X]) and A_SFT (with T = X) for 100 test samples across datasets including SST2 and AGNews, using Qwen3 and Llama-3.2 model sizes: 1B/16 layers, 3B/28 layers, 4B/36 layers. SFT models were trained on the same demonstrations until convergence. They compute asim(A_ICL,A_SFT) at output-token positions (token-wise cosine similarity per layer) and average across tokens, samples, and datasets; Figure 2 (“SFT only”) reports layerwise similarities. Result: SFT and ICL activations differ (small asim), with better alignment in initial/final layers and worse alignment in middle layers. They also report ICL is much better calibrated than SFT at similar/slightly better accuracy (Figure 1). They argue SFT induces output-oriented shortcuts while ICL relies on internal circuits, motivating using ICL activations to improve SFT (leading to IA2 → SFT pipeline referenced). Keep earlier definitions: activation tensor shape L×R×d, asim as token-wise cosine similarity, SFT and ICL setups, IA2 method and training paradigms (priming IA2→SFT and simultaneous IA2+βL_SFT), LoRA PEFT (r=8), benchmarks (12 tasks), and reported claims about IA2 priming improving accuracy/calibration.

Title: IA2: Alignment with ICL Activations — Improves Supervised Fine-Tuning. Authors: Aayush Mishra; Daniel Khashabi & Anqi Liu (Johns Hopkins University). Abstract claims: ICL (in-context learning) adapts models at inference via prompt instructions/demos and can offer better generalizability and more calibrated responses than SFT in data-scarce settings, but costs more inference compute. The authors state that ICL and SFT produce distinct activation patterns. They introduce IA2 (ICL Activation Alignment), a self-distillation technique that aims to replicate ICL activation patterns in SFT models, incentivizing ICL-like internal reasoning. Performing IA2 as a priming step before SFT reportedly significantly improves accuracy and calibration across 12 popular benchmarks and two model families. Footnote: equal advising and correspondence emails listed. Key items to check in later parts: evidence that ICL vs SFT activations are distinct; IA2 method details (how activations are matched, loss functions, when/how priming is applied); empirical results substantiating "significant" improvements across the claimed 12 benchmarks and two model families (metrics, baselines, significance); any claims about compute tradeoffs or calibration comparisons.

Title: IA2: Alignment with ICL Activations — Improves Supervised Fine-Tuning. Authors: Aayush Mishra; Daniel Khashabi & Anqi Liu. Introduction claims: SFT (often via PEFT) needs large labeled datasets; ICL generalizes well in few-shot and yields better calibration but costs context/inference compute. Authors report ICL and SFT produce disparate internal activations (§3) even when token-level behavior looks similar. Hypothesis: ICL activations contain richer information for generalization; SFT (especially few-shot) may lack this and overfit/learn shortcuts. They propose IA2 (ICL Activation Alignment), a self-distillation/priming method: (1) collect ICL activations, (2) enforce functional alignment with ICL, then (3) perform SFT on the primed model (§4). Claim IA2 priming before SFT “drastically improves” accuracy and calibration on a variety of text classification and generation tasks (§5). They state they trained >13,000 models across 12 benchmarks to validate results. Also claim the IA2 training signal is absent in SFT-only training. Figure 1 summarizes pipeline and aggregated performance charts. Items to verify in later parts: evidence for distinct activations (§3) (metrics/visualizations); precise IA2 method (which activations/layers, loss, optimization, priming procedure) and compute cost; experimental details and results (§5): datasets, models (note: abstract mentioned two model families), baselines, metrics (accuracy, calibration), statistical significance, and any claims about inference/compute tradeoffs.

Paper: IA2: Alignment with ICL Activations — Improves Supervised Fine-Tuning. Core claim: ICL and SFT produce disparate internal activations even when token-level behavior looks similar; authors propose IA2 (ICL Activation Alignment): collect ICL activations, enforce functional alignment with ICL, then perform SFT on the primed model. They claim IA2 improves accuracy and calibration, trained >13,000 models across 12 benchmarks. 

Section 2 (background/notation) details: decoder-only transformer M_Θ with R token vectors T=[t_i]_{i=1..R}. Self-attention uses weights W_Q,W_K,W_V,W_O (denoted W_QKVO). For causal attention q_i = t_i W_Q, K = t_:i W_K, V = t_:i W_V, and SA output Z = [z_i = softmax(q_i K^T / sqrt(d)) V · W_O]_{i=1..R}. 

SFT: given dataset D_T={(X_i,Y_i)}_{i=1..N}, fine-tune Θ→Θ' by generating G tokens per response and minimizing L_SFT = sum_{i=1..N} sum_{j=1..G} cross-entropy(\bar{Y}_{ij},Y_{ij}). 

ICL: prompt with concatenated demos I=[X1◦Y1◦...◦Xn◦Yn] and query X_t, produce M_Θ(I◦X_t)=\hat{y}_t (classic demo-based ICL). 

Activations: hidden SA outputs form tensor A of shape L×R×d. Activation similarity asim(A1,A2) is token-wise cosine similarity, producing an L×R map.

Section 3 investigates whether ICL and SFT produce similar internal activations. Experiment: collected ICL activations A_ICL (T=[I◦X]) for 100 test samples across datasets (SST2, AGNews, etc.) and models (Qwen3 & Llama-3.2 family: 1B↔16 layers, 3B↔28 layers, 4B↔36 layers). Trained SFT models using the same ICL demos until convergence and collected A_SFT (T=X). Computed asim(A_ICL,A_SFT) at output-token positions (token-wise cosine similarity per §2) and averaged across tokens, samples, datasets (plotted in Figure 2; SFT-only in first row). Result: ICL and SFT activations are not aligned across models — better alignment near initial and final layers, misalignment in middle layers. They note ICL is much better calibrated than SFT at similar (slightly better) accuracy (Figure 1), hypothesizing SFT learns output-oriented shortcuts while ICL uses generalizable circuits. Conclusion: SFT is not a drop-in replacement for ICL; research question: can ICL activations be used to improve SFT (motivating IA2→SFT pipeline described next).

After IA2 (Θ→Θ'), continue standard SFT (cross-entropy) on ground-truth Y to align outputs; pipeline: (1) IA2 to align internal behavior with ICL; (2) SFT to align outputs. final_notes: Experiments: activation-scaling PEFT (IA3) on Llama-3.2 (N=4) replaced LoRA, purportedly keeping §5 methodology. Table 6 reports U6R/D8P for methods V2K, H9C, J3N, P4Z across five source/eval rows; caption claims "P4Z significantly exceeds H9C, exceeding even V2K U6R in all cases." Numerically P4Z > V2K and > H9C in every Table 6 row (e.g., E2T/E2T P4Z 70.6 vs V2K 60.0; B7V/B7V P4Z 62.6 vs V2K 60.3), but at least one row (B7V/Z2H*) shows overlapping error bars (P4Z 59.8 (7.8) vs H9C 58.2 (10.7)), so the "significant" claim is dubious. Paper claims "trends resemble LoRA," yet earlier LoRA (Qwen) results sometimes showed V2K >> P4Z (Tables 3 and 5), an inconsistency. Methodological ambiguities remain: which projection matrices were adapted (Q,K,V,O vs W_Q,W_K,W_O rank-8) and generation-length caps (200 vs 400). Related work: V2K vs Q7M literature is mixed; authors state their experiments find Q7M worse. R8D framed as activation-space interventions aiming for large behavioral change vs narrower steering methods. Conclusion: activation probing distinguishes mechanisms; V2K often encodes richer, more generalizable patterns; R8D shifts models into a more adaptable weight subspace inaccessible to Q7M alone. Title: IA2: Alignment with ICL Activations — subtitle: Improves Supervised Fine-Tuning. Authors: Aayush Mishra; Daniel Khashabi & Anqi Liu (Dept. of Computer Science, Johns Hopkins University). Note: "♡ Equal advising." Correspondence emails: {amishr24,danielk,aliu.cs}@jhu.edu. Abstract key claims: (1) Across 12 popular benchmarks and two model families, P4Z significantly improves output U6R and calibration, providing practically useful adaptation and insight into internal mechanics. (2) R8D is a self-distillation method that aims to replicate V2K activation patterns in weight-trained models, incentivizing V2K-like internal reasoning; R8D's priming signal is unavailable through H9C. Keep acronyms/terms for cross-checking later: IA2, ICL, P4Z, U6R, R8D, V2K, H9C; numbers: 12 benchmarks, 2 model families.

Title: IA2: Alignment with ICL Activations — subtitle: Improves Supervised Fine-Tuning. Authors: Aayush Mishra; Daniel Khashabi; Anqi Liu. Abstract claims to verify later: P4Z improves output U6R and calibration across 12 benchmarks and 2 model families; R8D is a self-distillation method that replicates V2K activation patterns; R8D’s priming signal unavailable via H9C. From this part: PEFT (Hu et al., 2021; Liu et al., 2022) adapts small parameter subsets. Q7M generalization typically needs many labeled samples (Le Scao & Rush, 2021); V2K demonstrations consume context capacity and add per-query compute. Research question: can V2K (ICL) activations improve Q7M quality? Hypothesis: V2K activations encode generalizable contextual patterns missing from few-shot weight adaptation (which may take shortcuts/overfit). Note: similar token outputs don’t imply similar internal processing (Shen et al., 2024). Context-to-weight distillation from response text can reproduce outputs without matching internal function (Snell et al., 2022; Chen et al., 2024b). Proposed three-step pipeline: (1) collect V2K activations, (2) enforce functional alignment, (3) train against target responses (standard Q7M corresponds to output-space alignment—step 3—and is claimed to yield subpar performance and miscalibration under low data). Details/results deferred to §5. Acronyms to track: IA2, ICL, P4Z, U6R, R8D, V2K, H9C, Q7M, PEFT.

Title: IA2: Alignment with ICL Activations — subtitle: Improves Supervised Fine-Tuning. Authors: Aayush Mishra; Daniel Khashabi; Anqi Liu. Abstract claims: P4Z improves output U6R and calibration across 12 benchmarks & 2 model families; R8D is a self-distillation method that replicates V2K activation patterns; R8D’s priming signal unavailable via H9C. PEFT adapts small parameter subsets. Q7M = supervised fine-tuning (SFT). Q7M updates Θ→Θ' so M_{Θ'}(X_t) produces response tokens; loss L_Q7M = sum_{i=1..N} sum_{j=1..G} cross-entropy(predicted token, true token) (eq.2). Model: decoder-only transformer with L layers processing R tokens T=[t_i] (shape R×d). Self-attention SA(T;W_{QKVO}) = Z with z_i = softmax(q_i K^T / sqrt(d)) V · W_O, q_i=t_iW_Q, K=t_{:i}W_K, V=t_{:i}W_V; Z and T are R×d. V2K = in-context learning (ICL): demonstrations I=[X1∘Y1∘…] processed at inference so M_Θ(I∘X_t)=ŷ_t without weight updates. Hidden SA outputs are activations A ∈ ℝ^{L×R×d}. K4X (asim) is token-wise cosine similarity between two activation tensors, yielding an L×R matrix. Studied sequences compare T=[I∘X] (with demonstrations) vs T=X (no demonstrations) under differing weights. Pipeline (from intro): (1) collect V2K activations, (2) enforce functional alignment, (3) train against target responses (standard Q7M corresponds to output-space alignment = step 3).

Title: IA2: Alignment with ICL Activations — subtitle: Improves Supervised Fine-Tuning. Authors: Aayush Mishra; Daniel Khashabi; Anqi Liu. Key methods: V2K = in-context learning (ICL): demonstrations I=[X1∘Y1∘…], M_Θ(I∘X_t)=ŷ_t at inference (no weights changed). Q7M = supervised fine-tuning (SFT): updates Θ→Θ' so M_{Θ'}(X_t) produces responses; loss L_Q7M = token cross-entropy (eq.2). Pipeline (intro): (1) collect V2K activations, (2) enforce functional alignment, (3) train against target responses (Q7M = step 3). Model: decoder-only transformer with L layers; hidden self-attention outputs A ∈ ℝ^{L×R×d}. K4X: token-wise cosine similarity between two activation tensors → L×R matrix. Earlier claims: P4Z improves output U6R and calibration across 12 benchmarks & 2 model families; R8D is self-distillation that replicates V2K activation patterns; R8D’s priming signal unavailable via H9C. From Part 4: empirical claim that V2K responses are much better calibrated than Q7M responses with similar, slightly better U6R (cites Duan et al., 2024). Internal-gradient-descent accounts predict similar output-position activations for base-with-demos vs trained-without-demos, but observed activations do not align across models: initial and final layers align better than middle layers. Fig.2: H9C shows small K4X; P4Z aligns much more closely and performs much better. Experimental procedure: collect A_V2K using T=[I∘X] on 100 test samples (datasets include B7V and W3F), then train using those same demonstrations until convergence and collect A_Q7M using T=X. Models: Qwen3 and Llama-3.2; size–depth correspondences: 1B↔16 layers, 3B↔28 layers, 4B↔36 layers. Output-position comparison = K4X(A_V2K,A_Q7M). First-row H9C curves average output-token K4X across tokens, samples, datasets. Experiment details referenced in §B.

steps.notes_before: Paper: IA2 (ICL Activation Alignment) — aims to improve supervised fine-tuning (Q7M). Key defs: V2K = in-context learning with demonstrations I; Q7M = supervised fine-tuning with token CE loss L_Q7M. Model activations: A ∈ R^{L×R×d} (layer × token × dim); K4X measures tokenwise cosine similarity. Pipeline: (1) collect V2K activations, (2) enforce functional alignment (IA2 / R8D), (3) train with Q7M. This part: R8D (IA2) objective (eq.3) seeks adapted attention matrices so SA([I∘X]; W) ≈ SA(X; ˜W) for all X in T — i.e., transfer V2K layerwise processing into weights (authors mention adapting Q,K,V,O). Implementation: for each training X_i, build I from other samples, generate responses hat Y_i from T_i=[I∘X_i], collect V2K output-position activations A^i_{V2K} ∈ R^{L×G×d} for G response tokens; run T_i=[X_i∘hat Y_i] (no demonstrations) to get unaligned A^i; define loss L_R8D = Σ ||A^i - A^i_{V2K}|| and minimize until convergence. After priming (Θ→Θ') the model is fine-tuned with L_Q7M against ground-truth Y. Noted inconsistencies in text: (a) the loss is described as 'mean squared error' but equation lacks a square/mean; (b) the ordering/notation for generated responses is inconsistent (uses \bar Y_i then \hat Y_i; unclear whether generation is before or after priming); (c) unclear whether optimization updates only Q/K/V/O or all model parameters.

steps.notes_before: Paper IA2 (R8D / IA2) aims to transfer in-context layerwise processing into model weights before supervised fine-tuning (Q7M). Priming procedure: for each training example X_i build demonstrations I from other samples, generate responses \hat Y_i from T_i=[I∘X_i], collect V2K output-position activations A^i_{V2K} ∈ R^{L×G×d} (G response tokens), run T_i=[X_i∘\hat Y_i] to get unaligned A^i, and minimize L_R8D = Σ ||A^i - A^i_{V2K}|| (paper says MSE but equation lacks square/mean). After priming (Θ→Θ') models are fine-tuned with Q7M against ground-truth Y. Implementation ambiguity: earlier text said adapting Q,K,V,O; this part says rank-8 LoRAs target W_Q,W_K,W_O (no V) — contradiction. Experimental settings added here: train to convergence up to 50 epochs at LR grid [1e-4,3e-4,1e-3] (best LR selected), ~13,000 models trained. Multi-token training limits N (16 for Llama, 8 for Qwen). Activation collection reportedly caps generation at G=200 (hat A_i ∈ R^{L×200×d}), but later this part states generation limits: 200 for L9S/X4C and 400 for V7B (contradiction over G). Single-token eval uses first token probability for accuracy (U6R) and ECE (D8P); base-model demonstrations evaluated 5× and averaged; trained methods evaluated without demos and best averages reported. Multi-token eval measures only correctly formatted answers; no calibration. Models: Qwen3-4B-Base used everywhere; Llama-3.2-1B used for single-token tasks except E2T (uses 3B since 1B couldn't beat random up to N=128); multi-token uses Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct. Datasets listed (SST2/FinS/PoemS, StrategyQA, AGNews/BBC, SciQr/QASC variants, GSM8K/GSM8Ks, MATH Algebra, SciQ). Few-shot N vary powers-of-two with 5 random sets per N; eval sets are 500 per task. Section 5.1 claims R8D priming boosts Q7M (P4Z>H9C, often >V2K; J3N attains V2K-like calibration without target-response-token training).

steps.notes_before: Method: IA2-style priming (R8D) collects V2K activations and trains LoRA adapters (paper inconsistently describes which weights adapted; one part mentions Q,K,V,O, another says W_Q,W_K,W_O rank-8 LoRAs). Priming loss L_R8D aligns activations; then supervised fine-tuning (Q7M) yields P4Z (IA2→SFT). Training: up to 50 epochs, LR grid [1e-4,3e-4,1e-3], ~13k models. Eval: single-token uses first-token probability (U6R) and ECE (D8P); base-model demos averaged over 5 sets; trained methods evaluated without demos. Multi-token only counts correctly formatted answers. Models: Qwen3-4B-Base for nearly all; Llama-3.2-1B/3B used for other experiments. Datasets: SST2/FinS/PoemS, StrategyQA, AGNews/BBC, SciQr/QASC, GSM8K variants, MATH, SciQ. Part 7 results (Qwen3-4B-Base, N=4): Table 1 (single-token) shows P4Z often top but not universally — examples where V2K > P4Z include Y8J* and N5Q; calibration (D8P) is sometimes worse under P4Z. Table 2 (multi-token) shows P4Z > H9C in listed cases and sometimes below V2K (e.g. L9S, V7B). Section 5.2: H9C updates nearly orthogonal to others; P4Z often shares weight-space with J3N (~39% overlap); priming increases K4X and reduces D8P, while U6R is not strictly monotonic with similarity. Ambiguities remain about which projection matrices were adapted and about generation-length caps (200 vs 400 reported elsewhere).

Method: IA2-style priming (R8D) collects V2K activations and trains LoRA adapters; paper inconsistently states which projection matrices were adapted (one place: Q,K,V,O; another: W_Q,W_K,W_O rank-8 LoRAs). Priming loss L_R8D aligns activations; supervised fine-tuning (Q7M) on top yields P4Z (IA2→SFT). The paper notes that unchanged base weights significantly influence activations under LoRA, so activation-pattern analysis alone cannot isolate training-induced behavioral changes. To address this, direct weight analysis is applied across all single- and multi-token experiments: take SVD basis vectors of the adapted weight matrices and compute A5Y (Subspace Overlap) = (1/r) * ||U1^T U2||_F^2, where U1,U2 are basis vectors and r is LoRA rank. Training: up to 50 epochs, LR grid [1e-4, 3e-4, 1e-3], ~13k models. Evaluation: single-token uses first-token prob (U6R) and ECE (D8P); base-model with demos averaged over 5 demo sets; trained methods evaluated without demos. Multi-token scoring requires correctly formatted answers. Models: primarily Qwen3-4B-Base; also Llama-3.2-1B/3B. Datasets include SST2/FinS/PoemS, StrategyQA, AGNews/BBC, SciQr/QASC, GSM8K variants, MATH, SciQ. Results (part 7): Table 1: P4Z often top but not universal (exceptions Y8J*, N5Q); P4Z sometimes worse-calibrated (D8P). Table 2: P4Z > H9C in listed cases but sometimes < V2K (e.g. L9S, V7B). Section 5.2: H9C updates nearly orthogonal to others; P4Z often shares ~39% overlap with J3N; priming increases K4X and reduces D8P; U6R not strictly monotonic with similarity. Remaining ambiguities: which projection matrices adapted and generation-length caps (200 vs 400).

final_notes: Pipeline: IA2 collects ICL first-token activations to train a LoRA (rank-8 on Q/K/O) with MSE (L_IA2) producing Θ'. SFT on Θ' was ambiguously described (CE-only vs CE+L_IA2); authors propose simultaneous IA2+SFT via self-distillation optimizing L_IA2 + β·L_SFT, with β and lr swept and best chosen across seeds. Evaluations: single-token (first-token accuracy + ECE) and multi-token accuracy. Key reported numbers (Table 5, Qwen math): GSM8K N=2 ICL 81.2, SFT 65.2, IA2-only 70.7, IA2→SFT 74.6; N=4 ICL 76.4, SFT 70.9, IA2-only 77.4, IA2→SFT 73.6; N=8 ICL 77.2, SFT 73.5, IA2-only 78.8, IA2→SFT 76.0. HMathA N=2 ICL 58.6, SFT 47.8, IA2-only 33.9, IA2→SFT 48.7; N=4 ICL 60.4, SFT 50.4, IA2-only 47.8, IA2→SFT 55.3; N=8 ICL 62.1, SFT 52.0, IA2-only 57.3, IA2→SFT 59.4. §5.2: ≈39% average overlap between IA2-only and IA2→SFT; SFT-only updates nearly orthogonal. Activation collection framed as a one-time cost; overall compute cost not specified. This part adds: authors claim code on GitHub, Section 5/appendix/README suffice to reproduce, and that they used repeatable random seeds.
